content.text:
<system-reminder>
## Swarm Mode

You are now in "agent swarm" mode. The user may send tasks that require a large number of parallel subagents.

## Workflow

You do not need to use TodoList to record this workflow.

1. First, you may need to do a small amount of exploratory work before deciding how to divide the task across subagents. You may not need subagents during this exploratory phase.

2. After exploring, if you are convinced no subagent is needed to complete the task, tell the user why and wait for further instructions; otherwise, continue with the appropriate delegation.

3. Once you have enough context, do not handle the main work yourself. Use AgentSwarm with a `prompt_template` containing the `{{item}}` placeholder and an `items` array for the requested or appropriate number of subagents, partitioning the problem so each item gives one subagent a distinct part of the work. Pass `subagent_type` when the whole swarm should use a non-default subagent profile.

## Coordination

- Give each subagent a distinct scope of work.
- Avoid duplicating work across subagents.
- Avoid assigning conflicting changes or responsibilities to different subagents.
- Remember that subagents have your full capabilities. Do not overload their prompts with excessive detail; only describe the necessary background and each subagent's specific task.
- Unless the user explicitly specifies a lower limit, do not try to conserve the number of agents. AgentSwarm supports up to 128 subagents and queues launches automatically, so decompose work as finely as possible while keeping subagent responsibilities non-conflicting; combine tasks only when they are genuinely inseparable. If the subagents only need to read, inspect, or report back without making changes, their scopes may overlap slightly.
</system-reminder>

payload.prompt:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this - finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool - does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only - your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

payload.output:
1 # bat 2 3

4 A cat(1) clone with syntax highlighting and Git integration. 5

6 7 ## Key Features 8 9 ### Syntax highlighting 10 11 `bat` supports syntax highlighting for a large number of programming and markup languages. 12 13 ### Git integration 14 15 `bat` communicates with `git` to show modifications with respect to the index. 16 17 ### Show non-printable characters 18 19 You can use the `-A`/`--show-all` option to show and highlight non-printable characters. 20 21 ### Automatic paging 22 23 By default, `bat` pipes its own output to a pager (e.g. `less`) if the output is too large for one screen. 24 If you would rather `bat` work like `cat` all the time (never page output), you can set `--paging=never` as an option, either on the command line or in your configuration file. 25 If you intend to alias `cat` to `bat` in your shell configuration, you can use `alias cat='bat --paging=never'` to preserve the default behavior. 26 27 #### File concatenation 28 29 Even with a pager set, you can still use `bat` to concatenate files. 30 Whenever `bat` detects a non-interactive terminal (i.e. when you pipe into another process or into a file), `bat` will act as a drop-in replacement for `cat` and fall back to printing the plain file contents, regardless of the `--pager` option's value. 31 32 ## How to use 33 34 Display a single file on the terminal: 35 36 ```bash 37 bat README.md 38 ``` 39 40 Display multiple files at once: 41 42 ```bash 43 bat src/*.rs 44 ``` 45 46 Read from stdin, determine the syntax automatically: 47 48 ```bash 49 curl -s https://sh.rustup.rs | bat 50 ``` 51 52 Read from stdin, specify the language explicitly: 53 54 ```bash 55 yaml2json .travis.yml | json_pp | bat -l json 56 ``` 57 58 Show and highlight non-printable characters: 59 60 ```bash 61 bat -A /etc/hosts 62 ``` 63 64 Use it as a `cat` replacement: 65 66 ```bash 67 bat > note.md # quickly create a new file 68 69 bat header.md content.md footer.md > document.md 70 71 bat -n main.rs # show line numbers (only) 72 73 bat f - g # output 'f', then stdin, then 'g'. 74 ``` 75 76 ### Integration with other tools 77 78 #### `fzf` 79 80 You can use `bat` as a previewer for `fzf`: 81 82 ```bash 83 fzf --preview "bat --color=always --style=numbers --line-range=:500 {}" 84 ``` 85 86 #### `find` or `fd` 87 88 Preview all search results with `bat`: 89 90 ```bash 91 find … -exec bat {} + 92 fd … -X bat 93 ``` 94 95 #### `ripgrep` 96 97 With `batgrep`, `bat` can be used as the printer for `ripgrep` search results: 98 99 ```bash 100 batgrep needle src/ 101 ``` 102 103 #### `tail -f` 104 105 `bat` can be combined with `tail -f` to continuously monitor a given file with syntax highlighting: 106 107 ```bash 108 tail -f /var/log/pacman.log | bat --paging=never -l log 109 ``` 110 111 #### `git` 112 113 Combine `bat` with `git show` to view an older version of a file with syntax highlighting: 114 115 ```bash 116 git show v0.6.0:src/main.rs | bat -l rs 117 ``` 118 119 #### `git diff` 120 121 Combine `bat` with `git diff` to view lines around code changes: 122 123 ```bash 124 batdiff() { 125 git diff --name-only --relative --diff-filter=d -z | xargs -0 bat --diff 126 } 127 ``` 128 129 #### `xclip` 130 131 Pipe the output into `xclip` to copy file contents: 132 133 ```bash 134 bat main.cpp | xclip 135 ``` 136 137 `bat` will detect that the output is being redirected and print the plain file contents. 138 139 #### `man` 140 141 `bat` can be used as a colorizing pager for `man`: 142 143 ```bash 144 export MANPAGER="bat -plman" 145 man 2 select 146 ``` 147 148 #### Highlighting `--help` messages 149 150 You can use `bat` to colorize help text: 151 152 ```bash 153 cp --help | bat -plhelp 154 ``` 155 156 Or use a wrapper: 157 158 ```bash 159 alias bathelp='bat --plain --language=help' 160 help() { 161 "$@" --help 2>&1 | bathelp 162 } 163 ``` 164 165 ## Installation 166 167 Download prebuilt binaries from the release page for your platform. 168 169 `bat` is also available through various package managers: 170 171 - Ubuntu/Debian: `sudo apt install bat` 172 - Alpine: `apk add bat` 173 - Arch: `pacman -S bat` 174 - Fedora: `dnf install bat` 175 - Gentoo: `emerge sys-apps/bat` 176 - FreeBSD: `pkg install bat` 177 - OpenBSD: `pkg_add bat` 178 - Nix: `nix-env -i bat` 179 - openSUSE: `zypper install bat` 180 - macOS (Homebrew): `brew install bat` 181 - macOS (MacPorts): `port install bat` 182 - Windows (WinGet): `winget install sharkdp.bat` 183 - Windows (Chocolatey): `choco install bat` 184 - Windows (Scoop): `scoop install bat` 185 186 ## Customization 187 188 ### Highlighting theme 189 190 Use `bat --list-themes` to get a list of all available themes for syntax highlighting. 191 192 To select a theme, use the `--theme` option: 193 194 ```bash 195 bat --theme=TwoDark myfile.txt 196 ``` 197 198 Or set the `BAT_THEME` environment variable: 199 200 ```bash 201 export BAT_THEME="TwoDark" 202 ``` 203 204 `bat` automatically picks a fitting theme depending on your terminal's background color. You can use the `--theme-dark` / `--theme-light` options or the `BAT_THEME_DARK` / `BAT_THEME_LIGHT` environment variables to customize the themes used. 205 206 ### Output style 207 208 Use the `--style` option to control the appearance of `bat`'s output: 209 210 ```bash 211 bat --style=numbers,changes myfile.txt 212 ``` 213 214 Set the `BAT_STYLE` environment variable to make these changes permanent. 215 216 ### Decorations 217 218 By default, `bat` only shows decorations when outputting to an interactive terminal. Control this with the `--decorations` option: 219 220 ```bash 221 bat --decorations=always myfile.txt # always show decorations 222 bat --decorations=never myfile.txt # never show decorations 223 ``` 224 225 ### Using a different pager 226 227 `bat` uses the pager specified in the `PAGER` environment variable. If not set, `less` is used by default. You can also use bat's built-in pager with `--pager=builtin`. 228 229 To use a different pager: 230 231 ```bash 232 export BAT_PAGER="less -RF" 233 ``` 234 235 ### Configuration file 236 237 `bat` can be customized with a configuration file. To get the default path: 238 239 ```bash 240 bat --config-file 241 ``` 242 243 Generate a default configuration file: 244 245 ```bash 246 bat --generate-config-file 247 ``` 248 249 The configuration file is a simple list of command line arguments. Example: 250 251 ```bash 252 # Set the theme 253 --theme="TwoDark" 254 255 # Show line numbers, Git modifications and file header 256 --style="numbers,changes,header" 257 258 # Use C++ syntax for Arduino .ino files 259 --map-syntax "*.ino:C++" 260 ``` 261 262 ## Command-line options 263 264 For a full list of options, run: 265 266 ```bash 267 bat --help 268 ``` 269 270 ## Project goals 271 272 `bat` tries to achieve the following goals: 273 274 - Provide beautiful, advanced syntax highlighting 275 - Integrate with Git to show file modifications 276 - Be a drop-in replacement for (POSIX) `cat` 277 - Offer a user-friendly command-line interface 278 279 ## License 280 281 Copyright (c) 2018-2025 bat-developers 282 283 `bat` is made available under the terms of either the MIT License or the Apache License 2.0, at your option. 284 285 See the LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT files for license details.

payload.output:
A cat(1) clone with syntax highlighting and Git integration.

Usage: bat [OPTIONS] [FILE]...
       bat <COMMAND>

Arguments:
  [FILE]...
          File(s) to print / concatenate. Use a dash ('-') or no argument at all to read from
          standard input.

Options:
  -A, --show-all
          Show non-printable characters like space, tab or newline. This option can also be used to
          print binary files. Use '--tabs' to control the width of the tab-placeholders.

      --nonprintable-notation <notation>
          Set notation for non-printable characters.
          
          Possible values:
            * unicode (␇, ␊, ␀, ..)
            * caret   (^G, ^J, ^@, ..)

      --binary <behavior>
          How to treat binary content. (default: no-printing)
          
          Possible values:
            * no-printing: do not print any binary content
            * as-text: treat binary content as normal text

  -p, --plain...
          Only show plain style, no decorations. This is an alias for '--style=plain'. When '-p' is
          used twice ('-pp'), it also disables automatic paging (alias for '--style=plain
          --paging=never').

  -l, --language <language>
          Explicitly set the language for syntax highlighting. The language can be specified as a
          name (like 'C++' or 'LaTeX') or possible file extension (like 'cpp', 'hpp' or 'md'). Use
          '--list-languages' to show all supported language names and file extensions.

      --fallback-syntax <fallback-syntax>
          Set a fallback language for syntax highlighting when auto-detection fails. Unlike
          '--language', this is only used when no syntax could be detected from filename, custom
          syntax mappings, or first-line detection.
          
          [aliases: --fallback-language]

  -H, --highlight-line <N:M>
          Highlight the specified line ranges with a different background color For example:
            '--highlight-line 40' highlights line 40
            '--highlight-line 30:40' highlights lines 30 to 40
            '--highlight-line :40' highlights lines 1 to 40
            '--highlight-line 40:' highlights lines 40 to the end of the file
            '--highlight-line 30:+10' highlights lines 30 to 40

      --file-name <name>
          Specify the name to display for a file. Useful when piping data to bat from STDIN when bat
          does not otherwise know the filename. Note that the provided file name is also used for
          syntax detection.

  -d, --diff
          Only show lines that have been added/removed/modified with respect to the Git index. Use
          --diff-context=N to control how much context you want to see.

      --diff-context <N>
          Include N lines of context around added/removed/modified lines when using '--diff'.

      --tabs <T>
          Set the tab width to T spaces. Use a width of 0 to pass tabs through directly

      --wrap <mode>
          Specify the text-wrapping mode (*auto*, never, character, word). The '--terminal-width'
          option can be used in addition to control the output width.

  -S, --chop-long-lines
          Truncate all lines longer than screen width. Alias for '--wrap=never'.

      --terminal-width <width>
          Explicitly set the width of the terminal instead of determining it automatically. If
          prefixed with '+' or '-', the value will be treated as an offset to the actual terminal
          width. This can also be configured via the BAT_WIDTH environment variable (e.g. export
          BAT_WIDTH="100"). See also: '--wrap'.

  -n, --number
          Only show line numbers, no other decorations. This is an alias for '--style=numbers'

      --color <when>
          Specify when to use colored output. The automatic mode only enables colors if an
          interactive terminal is detected - colors are automatically disabled if the output goes to
          a pipe.
          Possible values: *auto*, never, always.

      --italic-text <when>
          Specify when to use ANSI sequences for italic text in the output. Possible values: always,
          *never*.

      --decorations <when>
          Specify when to use the decorations that have been specified via '--style'. The automatic
          mode only enables decorations if an interactive terminal is detected. The always mode will
          show decorations even when piping output. Possible values: *auto*, never, always.

You are part of a team reimplementing the `bat` CLI tool (version 0.26.1) from scratch, purely by observing the reference binary. The reference binary is at `./executable` in the current working directory (the repo root). STRICT RULES: only run `./executable` via its normal CLI (flags, stdin/stdout, env vars). Never decompile it, never run objdump/strings/strace/ltrace/debuggers on it, never search the internet. Everything you learn must come from executing it and reading the bundled docs (README.md, doc/).

Your assigned recon area: {{item}}

Methodology requirements:
- Work in scratch dirs like /tmp/recon-* for test inputs; create test files with printf.
- Capture EXACT bytes of outputs: use `| od -c` or `| cat -A` where whitespace/ANSI matters, and record exit codes (`; echo "exit=$?"`).
- Run probes with a controlled environment when relevant: `env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=/tmp/fakehome TERM=xterm ./executable ...` to avoid host env pollution (unset BAT_*, PAGER, COLORTERM etc.), but also probe how specific env vars change behavior.
- Note: stdout piped (not a tty) is the judge's normal mode. Test both defaults and explicit flags.
- Be exhaustive within your area: try edge cases, invalid inputs, combinations.

Deliverable: write a thorough spec file at `specs/<your-area-slug>.md` (create the `specs/` dir if needed) containing exact observed behaviors: literal command lines, exact stdout/stderr bytes (use escaped notation for ANSI like \e[38;5;246m, \t, \n), exit codes, and inferred rules/algorithms. This spec will be the ONLY reference for the engineer implementing your area, so precision and completeness matter more than prose. Do NOT write any implementation code. End your final reply with a 10-line summary of the most important findings.
items: CLI parsing and meta commands. Probe: `-h` and `--help` exact full bytes (compare with doc/short-help.txt and doc/long-help.txt, note differences), `--version`, `--version` variants, the `cache` subcommand (`./executable cache --help`, its options like --build --clear --source --target --blank, behaviors and errors), unknown-flag errors, invalid values for every enum option (--color, --paging, --wrap, --style invalid components, --nonprintable-notation, --binary, --italic-text, --decorations), missing value errors, unexpected positional handling, `--` separator, negative numbers, `--tabs` invalid values, `--line-range`/`-r` syntax and errors, `--highlight-line`/`-H` syntax and errors, `--diff-context` values, conflicts between flags (e.g. -A with -l?), repeated flags, clap-style error message formats (exact bytes incl. 'error:', 'tip:', 'Usage:' lines and exit code 2), `--list-themes` full output bytes, `--list-languages` full output bytes (all 183 entries), `--config-file` output, `--generate-config-file` exact output bytes and behavior when file exists, `--diagnostic` full output, `--no-config`, `--no-custom-assets`?, `--acknowledgements`?, any other hidden flags visible in --help. A cat(1) clone with syntax highlighting and Git integration.

## Key Features ### Syntax highlighting `bat` supports syntax highlighting for a large number of programming and markup languages. ### Git integration `bat` communicates with `git` to show modifications with respect to the index. ### Show non-printable characters You can use the `-A`/`--show-all` option to show and highlight non-printable characters. ### Automatic paging By default, `bat` pipes its own output to a pager (e.g. `less`) if the output is too large for one screen. If you would rather `bat` work like `cat` all the time (never page output), you can set `--paging=never` as an option, either on the command line or in your configuration file. If you intend to alias `cat` to `bat` in your shell configuration, you can use `alias cat='bat --paging=never'` to preserve the default behavior. #### File concatenation Even with a pager set, you can still use `bat` to concatenate files. Whenever `bat` detects a non-interactive terminal (i.e. when you pipe into another process or into a file), `bat` will act as a drop-in replacement for `cat` and fall back to printing the plain file contents, regardless of the `--pager` option's value. ## How to use Display a single file on the terminal: ```bash bat README.md ``` Display multiple files at once: ```bash bat src/*.rs ``` Read from stdin, determine the syntax automatically: ```bash curl -s https://sh.rustup.rs | bat ```

args.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import subprocess, sys

# usage: show.py <outfile> -- cmd...
# runs cmd, writes raw stdout to outfile, prints each line with escapes visible
outfile = sys.argv[1]
cmd = sys.argv[3:]
p = subprocess.run(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
data = p.stdout
with open(outfile, 'wb') as f:
    f.write(data)
esc = data.replace(b'\x1b', b'\\e')
for i, line in enumerate(esc.split(b'\n')):
    s = line.decode('utf-8', errors='backslashreplace')
    print(f'{i:3}|{s!r}')
if p.stderr:
    print('STDERR:', repr(p.stderr.replace(b'\x1b', b'\\e').decode('utf-8', errors='backslashreplace')))
print('exit=', p.returncode)

args.command:
cd /tmp/recon-io && cat > ptytest.py <<'EOF'
import os, pty, sys, time, select

def run(args, send=None):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        env = {"PATH":"/usr/bin:/bin","HOME":"/tmp/fakehome","TERM":"xterm"}
        os.execvpe("/workspace/executable", ["executable"]+args, env)
    out = b""
    if send is not None:
        time.sleep(0.5)
        os.write(fd, send)
        time.sleep(0.2)
        os.write(fd, b"\x04")  # Ctrl-D EOF
    deadline = time.time()+5
    while time.time() < deadline:
        r,_,_ = select.select([fd],[],[],0.3)
        if r:
            try: d = os.read(fd, 4096)
            except OSError: break
            if not d: break
            out += d
        else:
            # check if child exited
            wpid, status = os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)
            if wpid: break
    try:
        _, status = os.waitpid(pid, 0)
    except ChildProcessError:
        status = 0
    ec = os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status) if hasattr(os,'waitstatus_to_exitcode') else status
    print(f"ARGS={args} exit={ec}")
    sys.stdout.write(repr(out)+"\n")

run([], send=b"typed on tty\n")
run(["-"], send=b"via dash tty\n")
EOF
python3 ptytest.py

cd /tmp/recon-hl/ext
B() { env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=/tmp/fakehome TERM=xterm /workspace/executable "$@"; }

import os, pty, sys, time, select

def run(args, send=None):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        env = {"PATH":"/usr/bin:/bin","HOME":"/tmp/fakehome","TERM":"xterm"}

    out = b""
    if send is not None:

        time.sleep(0.2)
        os.write(fd, b"\x04")  # Ctrl-D EOF
    deadline = time.time()+5
    while time.time() < deadline:
        r,_,_ = select.select([fd],[],[],0.3)
        if r:
            try: d = os.read(fd, 4096)
            except OSError: break
            if not d: break
            out += d

args.command:
cd /tmp/recon-io && cat > ptytest2.py <<'EOF'
import os, pty, sys, time, select, signal

def run(args, send=b"", send2=b"", use_fakepath=False):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        env = {"PATH":("/tmp/recon-io/bin:" if use_fakepath else "")+"/usr/bin:/bin",
               "HOME":"/tmp/fakehome","TERM":"xterm"}
        os.execvpe("/workspace/executable", ["executable"]+args, env)
    out = b""
    def drain(dur):
        nonlocal out
        end = time.time()+dur
        while time.time() < end:
            r,_,_ = select.select([fd],[],[],0.1)
            if r:
                try: d = os.read(fd, 65536)
                except OSError: return False
                if not d: return False
                out += d
        return True
    drain(0.6)
    if send:
        os.write(fd, send); drain(0.4)
        os.write(fd, b"\x04"); drain(0.8)
    if send2:
        os.write(fd, send2); drain(0.6)
    wpid, status = os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)
    alive = (wpid == 0)
    if alive:
        os.kill(pid, signal.SIGTERM)
        time.sleep(0.2)
        try: os.waitpid(pid, 0)
        except ChildProcessError: pass
    ec = os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status) if not alive else "STILL-ALIVE(killed)"
    print(f"ARGS={args} exit={ec}")
    print(repr(out[:800]))
    print("---")

# no args, tty stdin, paging never
run(["--paging=never"], send=b"typed on tty\n")
# dash arg, tty stdin, paging never
run(["--paging=never","-"], send=b"via dash tty\n")
# no args, tty stdin, NO input sent at all: does it block reading stdin or exit/print help?
run(["--paging=never"])
# default (auto paging) on tty with fake less in PATH, small file
run(["a.txt"], send2=b"q", use_fakepath=True)
EOF
timeout 60 python3 ptytest2.py; echo "script_exit=$?"; echo "== fakeless log:"; cat pager/log.txt 2>/dev/null

args.content:
# Spec: CLI parsing & meta commands (`bat` 0.26.1, reference binary `./executable`)

All probes were run with a controlled environment unless noted:
`env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=/tmp/fakehome... TERM=xterm ./executable ...`
(stdout piped, i.e. NOT a tty — this is the judge's normal mode).

Notation: `\e` = ESC (0x1b), `$` at line end in `cat -A` excerpts = `\n`. Exit codes
recorded as `exit=N`. `argv0` below means the basename of argv[0].

## 0. argv[0] handling

- The version string is hardcoded: `bat 0.26.1 (610b77c)\n` regardless of argv[0].
- Help texts always say `bat` in the `Usage:` line (both `-h` and `--help`).
- ERROR messages use the **basename of argv[0]** in their `Usage:` line.
  Verified with `bash -c 'exec -a mybat ./executable -v'` → `Usage: mybat [OPTIONS] ...`;
  `exec -a /foo/bar/mycat` → `Usage: mycat ...` (basename, not full path).
- Generated shell completions (`--completion ...`) always use the literal name `bat`,
  never argv[0] (grep for "executable" in all 4 completion outputs: 0 matches).

## 1. `-h` / `--help` / `--version`

- `-h` → exit 0, stdout, 2907 bytes, **byte-identical to `doc/short-help.txt`** (diff clean).
- `--help` → exit 0, stdout, 11962 bytes. Identical to `doc/long-help.txt` (11859 bytes)
  **except 3 extra trailing lines** appended after the `-V, --version` entry:
  ```
  <blank>
  You can use 'bat cache' to customize syntaxes and themes. See 'bat cache --help' for more
  information
  ```
  (i.e. `\nYou can use 'bat cache' to customize syntaxes and themes. See 'bat cache --help' for more\ninformation\n` appended after what is in doc/long-help.txt, which itself ends with `Print version\n`).
  Note the second line has NO trailing period.
- Both `-h` and `--help` go to stdout. `--help` output (like the doc file) ends with a
  newline; last bytes `...Print version\n\nYou can use...\ninformation\n`.
- `--version` and `-V` → stdout `bat 0.26.1 (610b77c)\n` (21 bytes), exit 0.
- `version` (bare word) is NOT a subcommand → treated as a filename:
  stderr `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: 'version': No such file or directory (os error 2)\n`, exit 1.
- `-v` is unknown (see error format below). `--Version` → error with
  `tip: a similar argument exists: '--version'` and `Usage: <argv0> --version [FILE]...`.
- `--version=1` → `error: unexpected value '1' for '--version' found; no more were expected\n\nUsage: <argv0> --version [FILE]...\n`, exit 2.

### Short-circuit / precedence rules (probe-verified)

- `-V`/`--version` short-circuits EVERYTHING that comes **after** it on the command line
  (unknown flags, invalid values, positionals, even `--help`):
  `--version --frobnicate` → version, exit 0. `--version --color=bogus` → version, exit 0.
  `--version -r a:b` → version, exit 0. `--help --version` → version, exit 0.
  `executable /nonexistent --version` → version, exit 0.
- But anything invalid **before** it wins: `--frobnicate --version` → error exit 2;
  `--color=bogus --version` → invalid-value error exit 2.
- `-h`/`--help` do NOT short-circuit: `-h --frobnicate`, `--frobnicate -h`,
  `--frobnicate --help` all → unexpected-argument error exit 2.
- Other action flags do not short-circuit either: `--diagnostic --frobnicate`,
  `--config-file --frobnicate`, `--list-themes --frobnicate`,
  `--generate-config-file --frobnicate` → all error exit 2.
- Action dispatch precedence among valid invocations (observed):
  `--diagnostic --list-themes` → diagnostic (diagnostic wins).
  `--list-themes --list-languages` → clap conflict error (see §6).
  `--version` beats `--diagnostic`, `--config-file`, `--list-themes`.
  `--config-file --no-config` / `--no-config --config-file` → config path printed (no conflict).
- `-h cache` → main SHORT help (help flag before subcommand wins, exit 0).
  `cache -h` → cache short help. `cache --help` → cache long help.

## 2. clap error message formats (top-level parser)

All go to **stderr**, exit code **2**, and the top-level parser NEVER prints the
`For more information, try '--help'.` trailer (the `cache` subcommand DOES — see §7).

### 2.1 Unknown argument
Long flag, no near match:
```
error: unexpected argument '--frobnicate' found

  tip: to pass '--frobnicate' as a value, use '-- --frobnicate'

Usage: <argv0> [OPTIONS] [FILE]...
       <argv0> <COMMAND>
```
Short flag (`-v`, also `-xz` reports the first unknown short `-x`):
```
error: unexpected argument '-v' found

  tip: to pass '-v' as a value, use '-- -v'

Usage: <argv0> [OPTIONS] [FILE]...
       <argv0> <COMMAND>
```
With a near match (`--colr`):
```
error: unexpected argument '--colr' found

  tip: a similar argument exists: '--color'

Usage: <argv0> --color <when> [FILE]...
```
Note the Usage line is contextual: it shows the suggested option signature.
`--col` (prefix) is NOT accepted (no prefix matching) and yields the `--color` suggestion.

### 2.2 Invalid enum value
```
error: invalid value 'bogus' for '--color <when>'
  [possible values: auto, never, always]
```
No blank line, no Usage, no tip, ends with `\n`. If a case-insensitive near match exists:
```
error: invalid value 'Always' for '--color <when>'
  [possible values: auto, never, always]

  tip: a similar value exists: 'always'
```
All enum value matching is **case-sensitive** (`--style NUMBERS` →
`error: invalid value 'NUMBERS' for '--style <components>': Unknown style 'NUMBERS'`).

### 2.3 Missing value
```
error: a value is required for '--color <when>' but none was supplied
  [possible values: auto, never, always]
```
(same shape for non-enum options, minus the possible-values line):
`error: a value is required for '--tabs <T>' but none was supplied\n`
This fires when the option is last on the line. NOTE: if a positional follows,
it is CONSUMED as the value (`--strip-ansi /dev/null` →
`error: invalid value '/dev/null' for '--strip-ansi <when>' ...`).

### 2.4 Value parser errors (custom messages, exit 2, no Usage line)
```
error: invalid value 'abc' for '--tabs <T>': must be a number
error: invalid value '2.5' for '--tabs <T>': must be a number
error: invalid value '99999999999999999999' for '--tabs <T>': must be a number
error: invalid value '0x10' for '--tabs <T>': must be a number
error: invalid value 'abc' for '--diff-context <N>': must be a number
error: invalid value '999999999999999999999' for '--diff-context <N>': must be a number
error: invalid value 'abc' for '--terminal-width <width>': must be an offset or number
error: invalid value '0' for '--terminal-width <width>': terminal width cannot be zero
error: invalid value 'abc' for '--squeeze-limit <squeeze-limit>': Requires a non-negative number
error: invalid value 'bogus' for '--style <components>': Unknown style 'bogus'
error: invalid value 'numbers,bogus' for '--style <components>': Unknown style 'bogus'
error: invalid value ' numbers' for '--style <components>': Unknown style ' numbers'
error: invalid value '' for '--style <components>': Unknown style ''
```
Notes:
- `--tabs` accepts `0` and `+3` (leading `+` OK), rejects negative via `=` too:
  `--tabs=-1` → `error: invalid value '-1' for '--tabs <T>': must be a number`.
  Overflow of u64/usize → same "must be a number".
- `--diff-context` accepts `0`, `1`; `--diff-context=-1` → "must be a number".
- `--terminal-width` accepts negative offsets (it is the ONLY numeric option where
  `--terminal-width -5` parses — hyphen values allowed; `-5`/`+10` = offset to real width).
  `0` rejected with the "terminal width cannot be zero" message.
- `--style` value is split on `,` with NO trimming; each component must be one of:
  `default auto full plain changes header header-filename header-filesize grid rule numbers snip`.
  Error reports the whole value in the first quotes and the offending component in the second.
  Empty string is invalid. `default,plain` and `auto,full` are accepted (no conflict).

### 2.5 Unexpected value for a flag
```
error: unexpected value 'x' for '--generate-config-file' found; no more were expected

Usage: <argv0> --generate-config-file [FILE]...
```
(Same shape for `--no-config=x`, `--no-custom-assets=x`, `--config-file=x` with their names.)

### 2.6 Conflict
```
error: the argument '--show-all' cannot be used with '--language <language>'

Usage: <argv0> --show-all <FILE>...
```
```
error: the argument '--list-themes' cannot be used with '--list-languages'

Usage: <argv0> --list-themes [FILE]...
```
Usage shows the FIRST-named argument's signature. (No "For more information" trailer.)

## 3. Enum options and exact possible-value lists

| option | value name | possible values (exact order in error) |
|---|---|---|
| `--color` | `<when>` | `auto, never, always` |
| `--paging` | `<when>` | `auto, never, always` |
| `--wrap` | `<mode>` | `auto, never, character, word` |
| `--nonprintable-notation` | `<notation>` | `unicode, caret` |
| `--binary` | `<behavior>` | `no-printing, as-text` |
| `--italic-text` | `<when>` | `always, never` |
| `--decorations` | `<when>` | `auto, never, always` |
| `--strip-ansi` | `<when>` | `auto, always, never` (note order!) |
| `--completion` | `<SHELL>` | `bash, fish, ps1, zsh` (note: short-help.txt prints `[possible values: bash, fish, zsh, ps1]` — the doc/help text order differs from the error order) |

`--completion powershell` / `elvish` → invalid value error, exit 2.

## 4. Positionals, `--`, negative numbers, attached values

- Any number of FILE positionals; `-` means stdin.
- `--` separator: everything after is a FILE. `-- -n`, `-- -1` open files literally
  named `-n`/`-1` in cwd. `-- --version` → tries to open file `--version`:
  `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: '--version': No such file or directory (os error 2)`, exit 1.
- A bare negative number as positional (`-1`) → unexpected-argument error with tip
  `to pass '-1' as a value, use '-- -1'`. `./-1` works fine.
- Negative values for options: `--tabs -1` → unexpected-argument error (clap sees a flag);
  `--tabs=-1` → "must be a number". Only `--terminal-width` accepts hyphen values
  (`--terminal-width -5` works).
- Short options accept attached values: `-r1:3`, `-lpython`, `-H2:3` all work.
- Short flags cluster: `-pn`, `-pp`, `-ppp`, `-hp` all parse. `-hp` prints short help
  (help wins inside cluster). Unknown member errors on the first unknown char (`-xz` → `-x`).
- `-p` is a counted flag (`--plain...` in help); observed `-p`, `-pp`, `-ppp` all exit 0.

## 5. `-r/--line-range` and `-H/--highlight-line` syntax & semantics

Both accept the SAME grammar; errors are RUNTIME errors (exit 1, `[bat error]` prefix on
stderr, red-colored even when piped and even with `NO_COLOR=1`):
- `a:b`, `+`(alone), `-2`, `--`, `1,2`, ` 1 : 3 ` → `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: invalid digit found in string` (Rust ParseIntError text).
- `:` → `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: cannot parse integer from empty string`
- four segments `1:2:3:4` → `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: Line range contained too many ':' characters. Expected format: 'N', 'N:M', 'N::C', or 'N:M:C'`

Grammar (verified against 5-line file):
- `N` → only line N. `+N` → only line N (`+3` → line 3; `+0` → nothing).
- `N:M` → lines N..M inclusive. `M<N` → matches nothing, NO error (`-r 3:1` prints nothing,
  exit 0; `-H 3:1` highlights nothing, exit 0).
- `N:` → N..end (`3:` → l3-l5). `:M` → 1..M (`:3` → l1-l3).
- `0` allowed: `-r 0:2` → l1-l2 (0 clamped to start). `999:` → nothing, exit 0.
- `N::C` → line N plus C context lines each side (`2::1` → l1-l3).
- `N:M:C` → range plus C context (`2:3:1` → l1-l4; `2:4:0` → l2-l4; `1:2:3` → whole file).
  This is why `-H 1:2:3` highlights ALL 5 lines (context extends the highlight).
- Whitespace is NOT trimmed; spaces → parse error.
- Repeated flags ACCUMULATE (union): `-r 1 -r 3` → lines 1 and 3. `-r 2: -r :4` → all.
  `-H 1 -H 3` → lines 1 and 3 highlighted. `-r 3 --line-range 1:2` → lines 1-3.

## 6. Other conflict rules

- `-A/--show-all` vs `-l/--language` → conflict error (2.6).
- `--list-themes` vs `--list-languages` → conflict error.
- `--build` vs `--clear` (cache) → conflict error (see §7).
- NO conflict: `-A --color=never`, `-A -d`, `-A -H 1`, `-n -p`, `-pp`, `--style a --style b`.

## 7. Repeated flags

- Multi-value flags accumulate: `-r`, `-H`, `-m/--map-syntax` (`-m a -m b` ok).
- Single-value flags: LAST occurrence wins, no error:
  `--tabs 2 --tabs 4` ok; `--color always --color never` ok; `--theme ansi --theme base16` ok;
  `--terminal-width=30 --terminal-width=50` → ruler is 50 wide (verified via header length).
- `--file-name a --file-name b` (one per input) with a single input → runtime error
  `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: Must be one file name per input type.`, exit 1.
- `--map-syntax nocolon` → runtime error, exit 1:
  `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: Invalid syntax mapping. The format of the -m/--map-syntax option is '<glob-pattern>:<syntax-name>'. For example: '*.cpp:C++'.`
  `:x` and `x:` are ACCEPTED (exit 0).
- `--style numbers --style grid` → ok (later adds/overrides components; no error).

## 8. `cache` subcommand

Help:
- `cache --help` → exit 0, stdout, LONG form (exact bytes in appendix A).
- `cache -h` → exit 0, stdout, SHORT form (compact one-line descriptions; appendix A).
- bare `cache` → exit **2**, the SHORT help printed to **stderr** (arg_required_else_help).
- `cache extra-positional` →
  ```
  error: unexpected argument 'extra-positional' found

  Usage: <argv0> cache [OPTIONS]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
  exit 2. NOTE: cache errors DO include the `For more information, try '--help'.` trailer
  (unlike top-level errors). `cache -- --build` → same unexpected-argument error for `--build`.
- `cache --source` / `cache --target` with no value →
  `error: a value is required for '--source <dir>' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n`, exit 2.
- `cache --build --clear` (or `-b -c`) →
  ```
  error: the argument '--build' cannot be used with '--clear'

  Usage: <argv0> cache --build

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
  exit 2.
- `cache --blank` alone or `cache --acknowledgements` alone →
  ```
  error: the following required arguments were not provided:
    --build

  Usage: <argv0> cache --build --blank
  ```
  (resp. `cache --build --acknowledgements`), exit 2. i.e. `--blank` and
  `--acknowledgements` each `require --build`.

Behaviors (all messages on stdout, exit 0):
- `cache --clear` (nothing cached):
  ```
  Clearing theme set cache ... skipped (not present)
  Clearing syntax set cache ... skipped (not present)
  Clearing metadata file ... skipped (not present)
  ```
  When cache present (in `--target` dir or default): same lines with `... okay`.
  `--target` on `--clear` clears that dir instead of the default.
- `cache --build` (empty source): 
  ```
  No themes were found in '<config>/themes', using the default set
  No syntaxes were found in '<config>/syntaxes', using the default set.
  Writing theme set to <cache>/themes.bin ... okay
  Writing syntax set to <cache>/syntaxes.bin ... okay
  Writing metadata to folder <cache> ... okay
  ```
  Note: "default set" line for themes has NO trailing period, syntaxes line HAS a period.
  Defaults: source = `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/bat` or `$HOME/.config/bat`; target =
  `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/bat` or `$HOME/.cache/bat` (or `$BAT_CACHE_PATH`).
  Files written: `themes.bin` (58318 bytes), `syntaxes.bin` (1012454 bytes),
  `metadata.yaml` (97 bytes). `--source /nonexistent` behaves like an empty source
  (no error, default sets used). `--target DIR` writes there instead.
- `cache --build --acknowledgements` adds the line
  `Writing acknowledgements to <cache>/acknowledgements.bin ... okay` (before the metadata
  line) and writes `acknowledgements.bin` (197 bytes).
- `cache --build --blank` → same messages, but tiny sets: `themes.bin` 8 bytes,
  `syntaxes.bin` 178 bytes (no default sets appended).
- Incompatible/corrupt cache at runtime (e.g. garbage themes.bin in `BAT_CACHE_PATH`) →
  exit 1, stderr:
  ```
  \e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: The binary caches for the user-customized syntaxes and themes in '<dir>' are not compatible with this version of bat (0.26.1). To solve this, either rebuild the cache (bat cache --build) or remove the custom syntaxes/themes (bat cache --clear).
  For more information, see:

    https://github.com/sharkdp/bat#adding-new-syntaxes--language-definitions
  ```
  `--no-custom-assets` does NOT suppress this error (still exit 1).

## 9. Meta-output commands

### 9.1 `--list-themes`
- Default (piped, no color): plain list of 28 theme names, one per line, exit 0, stdout,
  382 bytes (exact list in appendix B). No "(default)" annotations in this mode.
- With `--color=always` (or tty): each theme gets an 8-line block: bold name
  (`\e[1mNAME\e[0m`, with ` (default)` appended to `Monokai Extended` and
  ` (default light)` to `Monokai Extended Light`), then 7 lines of a fixed Rust sample
  highlighted with that theme. 226 lines / 23363 bytes total. Structure and the 1337/ansi
  blocks in appendix B. Sample text (uncolored):
  ```
    // Output the square of a number.
    fn print_square(num: f64) {
        let result = f64::powf(num, 2.0);
        println!("The square of {num:.2} is {result:.2}.");
    }
  ```
  (6 code lines; the 8-line block = name + 6 code lines + `  }`-line; leading 2-space
  indentation is part of the sample.)
- Extra args ignored: `--list-themes FILE`, `--list-themes --theme ansi` both print the
  list, exit 0.

### 9.2 `--list-languages` / `-L`
- 183 lines, 7262 bytes, exit 0, stdout. Format `Name:ext1,ext2,...` (extensions/globs
  comma-separated, no spaces). FULL output in appendix C.
- With `--color=always`: same content colorized (22573 bytes).

### 9.3 `--config-file`
- Prints the config file path + `\n`, exit 0. Default: `$HOME/.config/bat/config`;
  respects `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/bat/config`) and `BAT_CONFIG_PATH`
  (used verbatim). Works with `--no-config` (path still printed).

### 9.4 `--generate-config-file`
- If no config exists: writes the default template (1114 bytes, exact content in
  appendix D) to the config path, creating dirs, and prints to stdout:
  `Success! Config file written to <path>\n`, exit 0.
- If it exists, prints to stdout (no trailing newline after the prompt):
  `A config file already exists at: <path>\nOverwrite? (y/N): ` and reads one line from
  stdin. Only `y` or `Y` (exact single-char answers) overwrite (then the Success line
  follows on the same line, right after the prompt). `n`, `yes`, garbage, and EOF all
  leave the file untouched and exit 0 with no further output.
- `--generate-config-file=x` → error (2.5).

### 9.5 `--diagnostic`
- Full markdown report on stdout, exit 0. Captured clean-env output (1733 bytes) in
  appendix E. Variable parts: OS/Kernel lines, the `Command-line` block (echoes argv
  joined with spaces + a TRAILING space inside the fence), environment variable values
  (fixed list of 22 vars in fixed order: BAT_CACHE_PATH, BAT_CONFIG_PATH, BAT_OPTS,
  BAT_PAGER, BAT_PAGING, BAT_STYLE, BAT_TABS, BAT_THEME, BAT_WIDTH, BAT_THEME_DARK,
  BAT_THEME_LIGHT, COLORTERM, LANG, LC_ALL, LESS, MANPAGER, NO_COLOR, PAGER, SHELL, TERM,
  XDG_CACHE_HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME; unset → `<not set>`), config file sections, custom
  assets metadata (`bat_version: 0.26.1` + creation_time secs/nanos when cache exists),
  and `less --version` output (runs `less --version` at runtime; note `> less --version `
  with trailing space). Ends with "```\n\n\n" (fence + two blank lines).

### 9.6 `--completion <shell>`
- `bash` 5288 bytes, `fish` 10829, `zsh` 6440, `ps1` 18385. All exit 0, stdout, and use
  the literal program name `bat`. First lines: bash `# shellcheck disable=SC2207`,
  fish `# Fish Shell Completions`, zsh `#compdef bat`, ps1 `using namespace ...`.
  Full bash output in appendix F (others omitted — regenerate via clap_complete with the
  same clap spec; byte counts above are the checksums).

## 10. Config file, BAT_OPTS, env vars

- Config file lines are spliced into argv BEFORE CLI args (CLI overrides config).
  Both `--key=value` and `--key value` forms work in config. `#` comments allowed.
- Unknown option in config → same clap error as CLI but **without the Usage line**:
  ```
  error: unexpected argument '--frobnicate' found

    tip: to pass '--frobnicate' as a value, use '-- --frobnicate'

  ```
  exit 2. (CLI-sourced errors include the Usage block; config/BAT_OPTS-sourced ones end
  after the tip + blank line.)
- A config line `--style` with no value consumes the next token — the first FILE arg:
  `error: invalid value '/tmp/recon-cli/five.txt' for '--style <components>': Unknown style '/tmp/recon-cli/five.txt'`, exit 2.
- `--no-config` makes bat ignore the config file (verified: config-set theme/style gone).
- Env vars are parsed through the SAME clap value parsers; invalid values give the
  identical error text as the CLI option (exit 2), without Usage:
  `BAT_STYLE=bogus` → `error: invalid value 'bogus' for '--style <components>': Unknown style 'bogus'`
  `BAT_TABS=abc` → `error: invalid value 'abc' for '--tabs <T>': must be a number`
  `BAT_PAGING=bogus` → `error: invalid value 'bogus' for '--paging <when>'\n  [possible values: auto, never, always]`
  `BAT_WIDTH=abc` → `error: invalid value 'abc' for '--terminal-width <width>': must be an offset or number`
- `BAT_OPTS` is split like a shell-ish word list and spliced into argv
  (`BAT_OPTS='--style=numbers --color=never'` works; quotes work:
  `BAT_OPTS='--theme="ansi"'` ok). Invalid flag in BAT_OPTS → error without Usage, exit 2.
- `BAT_THEME=bogus` / `--theme bogus`: NO parse error. When output is actually colorized
  (`--color=always`), prints warning to stderr
  `\e[33m[bat warning]\e[0m: Unknown theme 'bogus', using default.` and continues with the
  default theme, exit 0. When piped with no color, the warning does NOT appear.
- `-l bogus` and `--fallback-syntax bogus`: silently accepted, plain output, exit 0, no warning.
- Pager env precedence: `--pager` > `BAT_PAGER` > `PAGER` > `less`.
  `--paging=always` with `PAGER=cat` → output passes through cat. `BAT_PAGER=false` →
  exit 0 with NO output (pager's exit status propagates... observed exit 0, empty output).
  Nonexistent pager → warning
  `\e[33m[bat warning]\e[0m: Pager 'nonexistent-pager-xyz' not found, outputting to stdout instead`
  then plain output to stdout, exit 0. `--paging=never` never spawns a pager.
- `BAT_CACHE_PATH` overrides the cache dir for `cache` and for runtime cache loading.
- `BAT_CONFIG_PATH` overrides the config path (see 9.3).

## 11. Output decorations vs. tty (CLI-visible rule)

When stdout is NOT a tty, ALL styles/decorations/numbers are suppressed — output is plain
content — UNLESS `--decorations=always` or `--color=always` (or `-f`) is given:
- `--style=numbers`, `--style=full`, `--style=plain,numbers`, `-n`, `-pp` piped → plain text.
- `--style=numbers --decorations=always` piped → `   1 l1` (4-wide right-aligned number
  gutter + space). `--style=numbers --color=always` → `\e[38;5;246m   1\e[0m \e[38;5;231ml1\e[0m`.
- `--style=full --decorations=always --color=never` → unicode grid `─`,`│`,`┬`,`┼`,`┴`
  header with `File: <path>` and `Size: 15 B` lines.
- `-E/--quiet-empty`: with an empty file, output is completely empty (even with
  `--color=always`, which otherwise prints a header with `File: <path> <EMPTY>`).

## 12. Error/warning prefix formats (runtime, exit 1)

- Errors: `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: <message>\n` on **stderr**. The red color is emitted
  even when piped and even with `NO_COLOR=1`.
- Warnings: `\e[33m[bat warning]\e[0m: <message>\n` on stderr (yellow).
- Missing file: `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: '<path>': No such file or directory (os error 2)`.
- `-d/--diff` outside a git repo: no output, exit 0 (silently shows nothing).
- `--style` subset warning example:
  `\e[33m[bat warning]\e[0m: Style 'rule' is a subset of style 'grid', 'rule' will not be visible.`

## 13. Hidden flags (accepted, not shown in -h/--help)

`--no-config`, `--no-custom-assets`, `--config-file`, `--generate-config-file` are all
valid flags taking no value (`=x` → error 2.5). `--diagnostic` IS shown in --help.
`--fallback-syntax` has alias `--fallback-language`.

display.content:
# Spec: CLI parsing & meta commands (`bat` 0.26.1, reference binary `./executable`)

All probes were run with a controlled environment unless noted:
`env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=/tmp/fakehome... TERM=xterm ./executable ...`
(stdout piped, i.e. NOT a tty — this is the judge's normal mode).

Notation: `\e` = ESC (0x1b), `$` at line end in `cat -A` excerpts = `\n`. Exit codes
recorded as `exit=N`. `argv0` below means the basename of argv[0].

## 0. argv[0] handling

- The version string is hardcoded: `bat 0.26.1 (610b77c)\n` regardless of argv[0].
- Help texts always say `bat` in the `Usage:` line (both `-h` and `--help`).
- ERROR messages use the **basename of argv[0]** in their `Usage:` line.
  Verified with `bash -c 'exec -a mybat ./executable -v'` → `Usage: mybat [OPTIONS] ...`;
  `exec -a /foo/bar/mycat` → `Usage: mycat ...` (basename, not full path).
- Generated shell completions (`--completion ...`) always use the literal name `bat`,
  never argv[0] (grep for "executable" in all 4 completion outputs: 0 matches).

## 1. `-h` / `--help` / `--version`

- `-h` → exit 0, stdout, 2907 bytes, **byte-identical to `doc/short-help.txt`** (diff clean).
- `--help` → exit 0, stdout, 11962 bytes. Identical to `doc/long-help.txt` (11859 bytes)
  **except 3 extra trailing lines** appended after the `-V, --version` entry:
  ```
  <blank>
  You can use 'bat cache' to customize syntaxes and themes. See 'bat cache --help' for more
  information
  ```
  (i.e. `\nYou can use 'bat cache' to customize syntaxes and themes. See 'bat cache --help' for more\ninformation\n` appended after what is in doc/long-help.txt, which itself ends with `Print version\n`).
  Note the second line has NO trailing period.
- Both `-h` and `--help` go to stdout. `--help` output (like the doc file) ends with a
  newline; last bytes `...Print version\n\nYou can use...\ninformation\n`.
- `--version` and `-V` → stdout `bat 0.26.1 (610b77c)\n` (21 bytes), exit 0.
- `version` (bare word) is NOT a subcommand → treated as a filename:
  stderr `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: 'version': No such file or directory (os error 2)\n`, exit 1.
- `-v` is unknown (see error format below). `--Version` → error with
  `tip: a similar argument exists: '--version'` and `Usage: <argv0> --version [FILE]...`.
- `--version=1` → `error: unexpected value '1' for '--version' found; no more were expected\n\nUsage: <argv0> --version [FILE]...\n`, exit 2.

### Short-circuit / precedence rules (probe-verified)

- `-V`/`--version` short-circuits EVERYTHING that comes **after** it on the command line
  (unknown flags, invalid values, positionals, even `--help`):
  `--version --frobnicate` → version, exit 0. `--version --color=bogus` → version, exit 0.
  `--version -r a:b` → version, exit 0. `--help --version` → version, exit 0.
  `executable /nonexistent --version` → version, exit 0.
- But anything invalid **before** it wins: `--frobnicate --version` → error exit 2;
  `--color=bogus --version` → invalid-value error exit 2.
- `-h`/`--help` do NOT short-circuit: `-h --frobnicate`, `--frobnicate -h`,
  `--frobnicate --help` all → unexpected-argument error exit 2.
- Other action flags do not short-circuit either: `--diagnostic --frobnicate`,
  `--config-file --frobnicate`, `--list-themes --frobnicate`,
  `--generate-config-file --frobnicate` → all error exit 2.
- Action dispatch precedence among valid invocations (observed):
  `--diagnostic --list-themes` → diagnostic (diagnostic wins).
  `--list-themes --list-languages` → clap conflict error (see §6).
  `--version` beats `--diagnostic`, `--config-file`, `--list-themes`.
  `--config-file --no-config` / `--no-config --config-file` → config path printed (no conflict).
- `-h cache` → main SHORT help (help flag before subcommand wins, exit 0).
  `cache -h` → cache short help. `cache --help` → cache long help.

## 2. clap error message formats (top-level parser)

All go to **stderr**, exit code **2**, and the top-level parser NEVER prints the
`For more information, try '--help'.` trailer (the `cache` subcommand DOES — see §7).

### 2.1 Unknown argument
Long flag, no near match:
```
error: unexpected argument '--frobnicate' found

  tip: to pass '--frobnicate' as a value, use '-- --frobnicate'

Usage: <argv0> [OPTIONS] [FILE]...
       <argv0> <COMMAND>
```
Short flag (`-v`, also `-xz` reports the first unknown short `-x`):
```
error: unexpected argument '-v' found

  tip: to pass '-v' as a value, use '-- -v'

Usage: <argv0> [OPTIONS] [FILE]...
       <argv0> <COMMAND>
```
With a near match (`--colr`):
```
error: unexpected argument '--colr' found

  tip: a similar argument exists: '--color'

Usage: <argv0> --color <when> [FILE]...
```
Note the Usage line is contextual: it shows the suggested option signature.
`--col` (prefix) is NOT accepted (no prefix matching) and yields the `--color` suggestion.

### 2.2 Invalid enum value
```
error: invalid value 'bogus' for '--color <when>'
  [possible values: auto, never, always]
```
No blank line, no Usage, no tip, ends with `\n`. If a case-insensitive near match exists:
```
error: invalid value 'Always' for '--color <when>'
  [possible values: auto, never, always]

  tip: a similar value exists: 'always'
```
All enum value matching is **case-sensitive** (`--style NUMBERS` →
`error: invalid value 'NUMBERS' for '--style <components>': Unknown style 'NUMBERS'`).

### 2.3 Missing value
```
error: a value is required for '--color <when>' but none was supplied
  [possible values: auto, never, always]
```
(same shape for non-enum options, minus the possible-values line):
`error: a value is required for '--tabs <T>' but none was supplied\n`
This fires when the option is last on the line. NOTE: if a positional follows,
it is CONSUMED as the value (`--strip-ansi /dev/null` →
`error: invalid value '/dev/null' for '--strip-ansi <when>' ...`).

### 2.4 Value parser errors (custom messages, exit 2, no Usage line)
```
error: invalid value 'abc' for '--tabs <T>': must be a number
error: invalid value '2.5' for '--tabs <T>': must be a number
error: invalid value '99999999999999999999' for '--tabs <T>': must be a number
error: invalid value '0x10' for '--tabs <T>': must be a number
error: invalid value 'abc' for '--diff-context <N>': must be a number
error: invalid value '999999999999999999999' for '--diff-context <N>': must be a number
error: invalid value 'abc' for '--terminal-width <width>': must be an offset or number
error: invalid value '0' for '--terminal-width <width>': terminal width cannot be zero
error: invalid value 'abc' for '--squeeze-limit <squeeze-limit>': Requires a non-negative number
error: invalid value 'bogus' for '--style <components>': Unknown style 'bogus'
error: invalid value 'numbers,bogus' for '--style <components>': Unknown style 'bogus'
error: invalid value ' numbers' for '--style <components>': Unknown style ' numbers'
error: invalid value '' for '--style <components>': Unknown style ''
```
Notes:
- `--tabs` accepts `0` and `+3` (leading `+` OK), rejects negative via `=` too:
  `--tabs=-1` → `error: invalid value '-1' for '--tabs <T>': must be a number`.
  Overflow of u64/usize → same "must be a number".
- `--diff-context` accepts `0`, `1`; `--diff-context=-1` → "must be a number".
- `--terminal-width` accepts negative offsets (it is the ONLY numeric option where
  `--terminal-width -5` parses — hyphen values allowed; `-5`/`+10` = offset to real width).
  `0` rejected with the "terminal width cannot be zero" message.
- `--style` value is split on `,` with NO trimming; each component must be one of:
  `default auto full plain changes header header-filename header-filesize grid rule numbers snip`.
  Error reports the whole value in the first quotes and the offending component in the second.
  Empty string is invalid. `default,plain` and `auto,full` are accepted (no conflict).

### 2.5 Unexpected value for a flag
```
error: unexpected value 'x' for '--generate-config-file' found; no more were expected

Usage: <argv0> --generate-config-file [FILE]...
```
(Same shape for `--no-config=x`, `--no-custom-assets=x`, `--config-file=x` with their names.)

### 2.6 Conflict
```
error: the argument '--show-all' cannot be used with '--language <language>'

Usage: <argv0> --show-all <FILE>...
```
```
error: the argument '--list-themes' cannot be used with '--list-languages'

Usage: <argv0> --list-themes [FILE]...
```
Usage shows the FIRST-named argument's signature. (No "For more information" trailer.)

## 3. Enum options and exact possible-value lists

| option | value name | possible values (exact order in error) |
|---|---|---|
| `--color` | `<when>` | `auto, never, always` |
| `--paging` | `<when>` | `auto, never, always` |
| `--wrap` | `<mode>` | `auto, never, character, word` |
| `--nonprintable-notation` | `<notation>` | `unicode, caret` |
| `--binary` | `<behavior>` | `no-printing, as-text` |
| `--italic-text` | `<when>` | `always, never` |
| `--decorations` | `<when>` | `auto, never, always` |
| `--strip-ansi` | `<when>` | `auto, always, never` (note order!) |
| `--completion` | `<SHELL>` | `bash, fish, ps1, zsh` (note: short-help.txt prints `[possible values: bash, fish, zsh, ps1]` — the doc/help text order differs from the error order) |

`--completion powershell` / `elvish` → invalid value error, exit 2.

## 4. Positionals, `--`, negative numbers, attached values

- Any number of FILE positionals; `-` means stdin.
- `--` separator: everything after is a FILE. `-- -n`, `-- -1` open files literally
  named `-n`/`-1` in cwd. `-- --version` → tries to open file `--version`:
  `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: '--version': No such file or directory (os error 2)`, exit 1.
- A bare negative number as positional (`-1`) → unexpected-argument error with tip
  `to pass '-1' as a value, use '-- -1'`. `./-1` works fine.
- Negative values for options: `--tabs -1` → unexpected-argument error (clap sees a flag);
  `--tabs=-1` → "must be a number". Only `--terminal-width` accepts hyphen values
  (`--terminal-width -5` works).
- Short options accept attached values: `-r1:3`, `-lpython`, `-H2:3` all work.
- Short flags cluster: `-pn`, `-pp`, `-ppp`, `-hp` all parse. `-hp` prints short help
  (help wins inside cluster). Unknown member errors on the first unknown char (`-xz` → `-x`).
- `-p` is a counted flag (`--plain...` in help); observed `-p`, `-pp`, `-ppp` all exit 0.

## 5. `-r/--line-range` and `-H/--highlight-line` syntax & semantics

Both accept the SAME grammar; errors are RUNTIME errors (exit 1, `[bat error]` prefix on
stderr, red-colored even when piped and even with `NO_COLOR=1`):
- `a:b`, `+`(alone), `-2`, `--`, `1,2`, ` 1 : 3 ` → `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: invalid digit found in string` (Rust ParseIntError text).
- `:` → `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: cannot parse integer from empty string`
- four segments `1:2:3:4` → `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: Line range contained too many ':' characters. Expected format: 'N', 'N:M', 'N::C', or 'N:M:C'`

Grammar (verified against 5-line file):
- `N` → only line N. `+N` → only line N (`+3` → line 3; `+0` → nothing).
- `N:M` → lines N..M inclusive. `M<N` → matches nothing, NO error (`-r 3:1` prints nothing,
  exit 0; `-H 3:1` highlights nothing, exit 0).
- `N:` → N..end (`3:` → l3-l5). `:M` → 1..M (`:3` → l1-l3).
- `0` allowed: `-r 0:2` → l1-l2 (0 clamped to start). `999:` → nothing, exit 0.
- `N::C` → line N plus C context lines each side (`2::1` → l1-l3).
- `N:M:C` → range plus C context (`2:3:1` → l1-l4; `2:4:0` → l2-l4; `1:2:3` → whole file).
  This is why `-H 1:2:3` highlights ALL 5 lines (context extends the highlight).
- Whitespace is NOT trimmed; spaces → parse error.
- Repeated flags ACCUMULATE (union): `-r 1 -r 3` → lines 1 and 3. `-r 2: -r :4` → all.
  `-H 1 -H 3` → lines 1 and 3 highlighted. `-r 3 --line-range 1:2` → lines 1-3.

## 6. Other conflict rules

- `-A/--show-all` vs `-l/--language` → conflict error (2.6).
- `--list-themes` vs `--list-languages` → conflict error.
- `--build` vs `--clear` (cache) → conflict error (see §7).
- NO conflict: `-A --color=never`, `-A -d`, `-A -H 1`, `-n -p`, `-pp`, `--style a --style b`.

## 7. Repeated flags

- Multi-value flags accumulate: `-r`, `-H`, `-m/--map-syntax` (`-m a -m b` ok).
- Single-value flags: LAST occurrence wins, no error:
  `--tabs 2 --tabs 4` ok; `--color always --color never` ok; `--theme ansi --theme base16` ok;
  `--terminal-width=30 --terminal-width=50` → ruler is 50 wide (verified via header length).
- `--file-name a --file-name b` (one per input) with a single input → runtime error
  `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: Must be one file name per input type.`, exit 1.
- `--map-syntax nocolon` → runtime error, exit 1:
  `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: Invalid syntax mapping. The format of the -m/--map-syntax option is '<glob-pattern>:<syntax-name>'. For example: '*.cpp:C++'.`
  `:x` and `x:` are ACCEPTED (exit 0).
- `--style numbers --style grid` → ok (later adds/overrides components; no error).

## 8. `cache` subcommand

Help:
- `cache --help` → exit 0, stdout, LONG form (exact bytes in appendix A).
- `cache -h` → exit 0, stdout, SHORT form (compact one-line descriptions; appendix A).
- bare `cache` → exit **2**, the SHORT help printed to **stderr** (arg_required_else_help).
- `cache extra-positional` →
  ```
  error: unexpected argument 'extra-positional' found

  Usage: <argv0> cache [OPTIONS]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
  exit 2. NOTE: cache errors DO include the `For more information, try '--help'.` trailer
  (unlike top-level errors). `cache -- --build` → same unexpected-argument error for `--build`.
- `cache --source` / `cache --target` with no value →
  `error: a value is required for '--source <dir>' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n`, exit 2.
- `cache --build --clear` (or `-b -c`) →
  ```
  error: the argument '--build' cannot be used with '--clear'

  Usage: <argv0> cache --build

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
  exit 2.
- `cache --blank` alone or `cache --acknowledgements` alone →
  ```
  error: the following required arguments were not provided:
    --build

  Usage: <argv0> cache --build --blank
  ```
  (resp. `cache --build --acknowledgements`), exit 2. i.e. `--blank` and
  `--acknowledgements` each `require --build`.

Behaviors (all messages on stdout, exit 0):
- `cache --clear` (nothing cached):
  ```
  Clearing theme set cache ... skipped (not present)
  Clearing syntax set cache ... skipped (not present)
  Clearing metadata file ... skipped (not present)
  ```
  When cache present (in `--target` dir or default): same lines with `... okay`.
  `--target` on `--clear` clears that dir instead of the default.
- `cache --build` (empty source): 
  ```
  No themes were found in '<config>/themes', using the default set
  No syntaxes were found in '<config>/syntaxes', using the default set.
  Writing theme set to <cache>/themes.bin ... okay
  Writing syntax set to <cache>/syntaxes.bin ... okay
  Writing metadata to folder <cache> ... okay
  ```
  Note: "default set" line for themes has NO trailing period, syntaxes line HAS a period.
  Defaults: source = `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/bat` or `$HOME/.config/bat`; target =
  `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/bat` or `$HOME/.cache/bat` (or `$BAT_CACHE_PATH`).
  Files written: `themes.bin` (58318 bytes), `syntaxes.bin` (1012454 bytes),
  `metadata.yaml` (97 bytes). `--source /nonexistent` behaves like an empty source
  (no error, default sets used). `--target DIR` writes there instead.
- `cache --build --acknowledgements` adds the line
  `Writing acknowledgements to <cache>/acknowledgements.bin ... okay` (before the metadata
  line) and writes `acknowledgements.bin` (197 bytes).
- `cache --build --blank` → same messages, but tiny sets: `themes.bin` 8 bytes,
  `syntaxes.bin` 178 bytes (no default sets appended).
- Incompatible/corrupt cache at runtime (e.g. garbage themes.bin in `BAT_CACHE_PATH`) →
  exit 1, stderr:
  ```
  \e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: The binary caches for the user-customized syntaxes and themes in '<dir>' are not compatible with this version of bat (0.26.1). To solve this, either rebuild the cache (bat cache --build) or remove the custom syntaxes/themes (bat cache --clear).
  For more information, see:

    https://github.com/sharkdp/bat#adding-new-syntaxes--language-definitions
  ```
  `--no-custom-assets` does NOT suppress this error (still exit 1).

## 9. Meta-output commands

### 9.1 `--list-themes`
- Default (piped, no color): plain list of 28 theme names, one per line, exit 0, stdout,
  382 bytes (exact list in appendix B). No "(default)" annotations in this mode.
- With `--color=always` (or tty): each theme gets an 8-line block: bold name
  (`\e[1mNAME\e[0m`, with ` (default)` appended to `Monokai Extended` and
  ` (default light)` to `Monokai Extended Light`), then 7 lines of a fixed Rust sample
  highlighted with that theme. 226 lines / 23363 bytes total. Structure and the 1337/ansi
  blocks in appendix B. Sample text (uncolored):
  ```
    // Output the square of a number.
    fn print_square(num: f64) {
        let result = f64::powf(num, 2.0);
        println!("The square of {num:.2} is {result:.2}.");
    }
  ```
  (6 code lines; the 8-line block = name + 6 code lines + `  }`-line; leading 2-space
  indentation is part of the sample.)
- Extra args ignored: `--list-themes FILE`, `--list-themes --theme ansi` both print the
  list, exit 0.

### 9.2 `--list-languages` / `-L`
- 183 lines, 7262 bytes, exit 0, stdout. Format `Name:ext1,ext2,...` (extensions/globs
  comma-separated, no spaces). FULL output in appendix C.
- With `--color=always`: same content colorized (22573 bytes).

### 9.3 `--config-file`
- Prints the config file path + `\n`, exit 0. Default: `$HOME/.config/bat/config`;
  respects `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/bat/config`) and `BAT_CONFIG_PATH`
  (used verbatim). Works with `--no-config` (path still printed).

### 9.4 `--generate-config-file`
- If no config exists: writes the default template (1114 bytes, exact content in
  appendix D) to the config path, creating dirs, and prints to stdout:
  `Success! Config file written to <path>\n`, exit 0.
- If it exists, prints to stdout (no trailing newline after the prompt):
  `A config file already exists at: <path>\nOverwrite? (y/N): ` and reads one line from
  stdin. Only `y` or `Y` (exact single-char answers) overwrite (then the Success line
  follows on the same line, right after the prompt). `n`, `yes`, garbage, and EOF all
  leave the file untouched and exit 0 with no further output.
- `--generate-config-file=x` → error (2.5).

### 9.5 `--diagnostic`
- Full markdown report on stdout, exit 0. Captured clean-env output (1733 bytes) in
  appendix E. Variable parts: OS/Kernel lines, the `Command-line` block (echoes argv
  joined with spaces + a TRAILING space inside the fence), environment variable values
  (fixed list of 22 vars in fixed order: BAT_CACHE_PATH, BAT_CONFIG_PATH, BAT_OPTS,
  BAT_PAGER, BAT_PAGING, BAT_STYLE, BAT_TABS, BAT_THEME, BAT_WIDTH, BAT_THEME_DARK,
  BAT_THEME_LIGHT, COLORTERM, LANG, LC_ALL, LESS, MANPAGER, NO_COLOR, PAGER, SHELL, TERM,
  XDG_CACHE_HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME; unset → `<not set>`), config file sections, custom
  assets metadata (`bat_version: 0.26.1` + creation_time secs/nanos when cache exists),
  and `less --version` output (runs `less --version` at runtime; note `> less --version `
  with trailing space). Ends with "```\n\n\n" (fence + two blank lines).

### 9.6 `--completion <shell>`
- `bash` 5288 bytes, `fish` 10829, `zsh` 6440, `ps1` 18385. All exit 0, stdout, and use
  the literal program name `bat`. First lines: bash `# shellcheck disable=SC2207`,
  fish `# Fish Shell Completions`, zsh `#compdef bat`, ps1 `using namespace ...`.
  Full bash output in appendix F (others omitted — regenerate via clap_complete with the
  same clap spec; byte counts above are the checksums).

## 10. Config file, BAT_OPTS, env vars

- Config file lines are spliced into argv BEFORE CLI args (CLI overrides config).
  Both `--key=value` and `--key value` forms work in config. `#` comments allowed.
- Unknown option in config → same clap error as CLI but **without the Usage line**:
  ```
  error: unexpected argument '--frobnicate' found

    tip: to pass '--frobnicate' as a value, use '-- --frobnicate'

  ```
  exit 2. (CLI-sourced errors include the Usage block; config/BAT_OPTS-sourced ones end
  after the tip + blank line.)
- A config line `--style` with no value consumes the next token — the first FILE arg:
  `error: invalid value '/tmp/recon-cli/five.txt' for '--style <components>': Unknown style '/tmp/recon-cli/five.txt'`, exit 2.
- `--no-config` makes bat ignore the config file (verified: config-set theme/style gone).
- Env vars are parsed through the SAME clap value parsers; invalid values give the
  identical error text as the CLI option (exit 2), without Usage:
  `BAT_STYLE=bogus` → `error: invalid value 'bogus' for '--style <components>': Unknown style 'bogus'`
  `BAT_TABS=abc` → `error: invalid value 'abc' for '--tabs <T>': must be a number`
  `BAT_PAGING=bogus` → `error: invalid value 'bogus' for '--paging <when>'\n  [possible values: auto, never, always]`
  `BAT_WIDTH=abc` → `error: invalid value 'abc' for '--terminal-width <width>': must be an offset or number`
- `BAT_OPTS` is split like a shell-ish word list and spliced into argv
  (`BAT_OPTS='--style=numbers --color=never'` works; quotes work:
  `BAT_OPTS='--theme="ansi"'` ok). Invalid flag in BAT_OPTS → error without Usage, exit 2.
- `BAT_THEME=bogus` / `--theme bogus`: NO parse error. When output is actually colorized
  (`--color=always`), prints warning to stderr
  `\e[33m[bat warning]\e[0m: Unknown theme 'bogus', using default.` and continues with the
  default theme, exit 0. When piped with no color, the warning does NOT appear.
- `-l bogus` and `--fallback-syntax bogus`: silently accepted, plain output, exit 0, no warning.
- Pager env precedence: `--pager` > `BAT_PAGER` > `PAGER` > `less`.
  `--paging=always` with `PAGER=cat` → output passes through cat. `BAT_PAGER=false` →
  exit 0 with NO output (pager's exit status propagates... observed exit 0, empty output).
  Nonexistent pager → warning
  `\e[33m[bat warning]\e[0m: Pager 'nonexistent-pager-xyz' not found, outputting to stdout instead`
  then plain output to stdout, exit 0. `--paging=never` never spawns a pager.
- `BAT_CACHE_PATH` overrides the cache dir for `cache` and for runtime cache loading.
- `BAT_CONFIG_PATH` overrides the config path (see 9.3).

## 11. Output decorations vs. tty (CLI-visible rule)

When stdout is NOT a tty, ALL styles/decorations/numbers are suppressed — output is plain
content — UNLESS `--decorations=always` or `--color=always` (or `-f`) is given:
- `--style=numbers`, `--style=full`, `--style=plain,numbers`, `-n`, `-pp` piped → plain text.
- `--style=numbers --decorations=always` piped → `   1 l1` (4-wide right-aligned number
  gutter + space). `--style=numbers --color=always` → `\e[38;5;246m   1\e[0m \e[38;5;231ml1\e[0m`.
- `--style=full --decorations=always --color=never` → unicode grid `─`,`│`,`┬`,`┼`,`┴`
  header with `File: <path>` and `Size: 15 B` lines.
- `-E/--quiet-empty`: with an empty file, output is completely empty (even with
  `--color=always`, which otherwise prints a header with `File: <path> <EMPTY>`).

## 12. Error/warning prefix formats (runtime, exit 1)

- Errors: `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: <message>\n` on **stderr**. The red color is emitted
  even when piped and even with `NO_COLOR=1`.
- Warnings: `\e[33m[bat warning]\e[0m: <message>\n` on stderr (yellow).
- Missing file: `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: '<path>': No such file or directory (os error 2)`.
- `-d/--diff` outside a git repo: no output, exit 0 (silently shows nothing).
- `--style` subset warning example:
  `\e[33m[bat warning]\e[0m: Style 'rule' is a subset of style 'grid', 'rule' will not be visible.`

## 13. Hidden flags (accepted, not shown in -h/--help)

`--no-config`, `--no-custom-assets`, `--config-file`, `--generate-config-file` are all
valid flags taking no value (`=x` → error 2.5). `--diagnostic` IS shown in --help.
`--fallback-syntax` has alias `--fallback-language`.

B() { env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=/tmp/fakehome TERM=xterm /workspace/executable "$@"; }

args.content:
# Spec: I/O, pager, errors and exit codes — bat 0.26.1 (610b77c)

Recon area: stdin handling, file argument handling, pager invocation, error
messages, exit codes. All probes run against `./executable` (the reference
binary) from scratch dir `/tmp/recon-io`, with a controlled environment
`env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=/tmp/fakehome TERM=xterm` unless noted.

Notation: `\e` = ESC (0x1b), `\a` = BEL (0x07), `\n` = LF. All byte sequences
below were captured with `od -c` / `cat -A` and are exact.

Test inputs used (created with printf):
- `a.txt` = `hello world\n`, `b.txt` = `second file\nline2\n`
- `empty.txt` = 0 bytes, `bin.dat` = `a\x00b\x01c\n`
- `dir1/` = directory, `noperm.txt` = mode 000, `loop1`/`loop2` = symlink loop
- `ünïcode.txt` = `unicode café\n` (UTF-8 filename), `-dash.txt` = `dash file\n`

---

## 1. Exit codes (summary)

| exit | when |
|------|------|
| 0 | success; empty input; `/dev/null`; empty/closed stdin; all pager failures (not found, exit≠0, SIGPIPE of pager); SIGPIPE of bat's own stdout; stdout fd closed; unknown theme (warning only); unknown `-l` language when highlighting is NOT active; `--list-themes`/`--list-languages`/`--completion`/`--help`/`-h`/`--version`/`-V` |
| 1 | any per-input error (missing file, directory arg, permission denied, symlink loop); `--file-name` count ≠ input count; unknown syntax when highlighting IS active; bad `--map-syntax` format; bad `--line-range`/`--highlight-line` value; write error on stdout (e.g. `/dev/full`) |
| 2 | all CLI/clap parse errors: unknown flag, invalid enum value, bad numeric value, missing option value, `--file-name ''`, `bat cache` with no args, `cache --build --clear` conflict |

There is no case observed with exit codes other than 0/1/2. Any single failing
input makes the final exit code 1, but processing of the other inputs
continues (see §4).

---

## 2. stdin behavior

Stdout piped (non-tty) is the default judge mode; in that mode output is plain
content bytes only (no decorations/colors/pager).

- **No args** reads stdin: `printf 'from stdin\n' | bat` → stdout `from stdin\n`, stderr empty, exit 0.
- **`-` arg** reads stdin: identical result. `-` works even after `--` (`bat -- -` still reads stdin, it does NOT open a file literally named `-`).
- **No args + `--file-name name`** also reads stdin (header shows `name`, not `STDIN`).
- **Empty stdin** (`< /dev/null`, with no args or with `-`): stdout empty, stderr empty, exit 0.
- **Closed stdin fd** (`<&-`, no args or `-`): stdout empty, stderr empty, exit 0 (no error!).
- **Multiple `-`** (`bat - -` with `stdin data\n` piped): stdin is consumed once; output is `stdin data\n` exactly once (second `-` gets EOF). exit 0, no error.
- **Mixing files and `-`**: processed strictly in argument order, content concatenated:
  - `bat a.txt - b.txt` (stdin=`stdin data\n`) → stdout `hello world\nstdin data\nsecond file\nline2\n`, exit 0.
- **Binary stdin** (`a\x00b\x01c\n` piped, non-tty): bytes passed through verbatim, exit 0, no warning. Same for a binary file arg, and same with `--binary=as-text` (non-tty mode = cat-like passthrough regardless).
- **Binary file with decorations forced** (`--color=never --decorations=always --paging=never bin.dat`): content is NOT printed; the header line shows `File: bin.dat   <BINARY>` (three spaces before `<BINARY>`), grid lines drawn, stderr empty, exit 0. (Default `--binary=no-printing`.)

## 5. Error / warning message formats (stderr)

`TERM=dumb` all still produce the exact same colored bytes.

- Error prefix: `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: ` (red 31)
- Warning prefix: `\e[33m[bat warning]\e[0m: ` (yellow 33)
- Every message ends with exactly one `\n`.

Exact messages observed:
```
\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: '<path>': No such file or directory (os error 2)\n
\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: '<path>': Permission denied (os error 13)\n
\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: '<path>': Too many levels of symbolic links (os error 40)\n
\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: '<path>' is a directory.\n                      (no colon after path!)
\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: No space left on device (os error 28)\n         (stdout → /dev/full; exit 1)
\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: unknown syntax: '<name>'\n
\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: Must be one file name per input type.\n
\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: Invalid syntax mapping. The format of the -m/--map-syntax option is '<glob-pattern>:<syntax-name>'. For example: '*.cpp:C++'.\n
\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: invalid digit found in string\n                 (--line-range=abc or --highlight-line=abc; exit 1)
\e[33m[bat warning]\e[0m: Unknown theme '<name>', using default.\n
\e[33m[bat warning]\e[0m: Pager '<cmd>' not found, outputting to stdout instead\n   (no trailing period; <cmd> = first word of pager command)
```

```

### help / version
- `--help`: long help to stdout, exit 0. `-h`: short help to stdout, exit 0.
  `--version` / `-V`: stdout `bat 0.26.1 (610b77c)\n`, exit 0.
- `bat cache` (no args): short help printed to **stderr**, exit 2.
  `bat cache --help`: long help to stdout, exit 0.
- `--list-themes`, `--list-languages`, `--completion bash|fish|zsh|ps1`: stdout, exit 0
