args.content:
# Spec: Content transformations (bat 0.26.1, binary `610b77c`)

Recon area: `-A/--show-all`, `--nonprintable-notation`, `--tabs`, `--wrap`, `-r/--line-range`,
`-H/--highlight-line`, `-s/--squeeze-blank`/`--squeeze-limit`, `--strip-ansi`, binary handling,
encodings (invalid UTF-8, BOM, UTF-16, CRLF), missing trailing newline, empty input, long lines.

All probes used a scrubbed environment unless noted:

```
env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=/tmp/fakehome TERM=xterm ./executable <args>
```

stdout was a pipe in all probes (the judge's normal mode). `--paging=never` was passed for safety
(paging never engages when stdout is not a tty anyway).

## 0. The three output paths (fundamental)

Behavior depends on which of three paths is taken:

1. **Plain passthrough path** — stdout piped AND no `--color=always`/`-f` AND no
   `--decorations=always` (default piped style is plain) AND no `-A`:
   the input bytes are copied **byte-for-byte** to stdout. In this mode ALL of
   `--tabs`, `--wrap`, `--terminal-width`, `--strip-ansi`, `--binary`, invalid-UTF-8
   replacement and BOM stripping are **ignored**. `-s/--squeeze-blank` and `-r/--line-range`
   **do** still apply in this mode.
2. **ANSI printer path** — `--color=always` (or tty): content re-emitted with ANSI styles,
   wrapping, tab expansion, UTF-8 sanitizing, BOM handling, binary suppression all active.
3. **Decorations path** — `--decorations=always` (or tty): grid/numbers/header printed;
   content transformation active even without color.

`-A` forces a transforming printer path even when piped plain (but does not add
decorations or colors by itself).

Default when piped: style = plain, color = off → path 1. Verified:
`printf 'hello\nworld\n' > plain.txt; ./executable plain.txt` → stdout `hello\nworld\n`, exit 0.

Default terminal width when piped (no COLUMNS/BAT_WIDTH honored): **80**.
`COLUMNS=30` had no effect; `BAT_WIDTH=30` did (grid became 30 wide).

## 1. `-A/--show-all` and `--nonprintable-notation`

Long flag `--show-all` confirmed working. `--nonprintable-notation` accepts only
`unicode` (default) and `caret`; any other value → clap error, exit 2:

```
error: invalid value 'foo' for '--nonprintable-notation <notation>'
  [possible values: unicode, caret]
```

### 1.1 Replacement mapping (both notations unless noted)

Input is treated as raw bytes/UTF-8; replacement is per character:

| Input | unicode notation | caret notation |
|---|---|---|
| 0x00–0x08, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x0E–0x1F (C0 except \t,\n,\r) | U+2400+codepoint (␀…␟), single glyph | `^@`…`^_` (caret + codepoint+0x40), 2 ASCII chars |
| 0x09 TAB | tab placeholder (see §2): `├`+`─`*n+`┤`, or `↹` (U+21B9) if width 1 | same as unicode |
| 0x0A LF | `␊` (U+240A) followed by real `\n` | `^J` followed by real `\n` |
| 0x0D CR | `␍` (U+240D), inline (no line break) | `^M` |
| 0x20 SPACE | `·` (U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT) | `·` (same) |
| 0x7F DEL | `␡` (U+2421) | `^?` |
| 0x21–0x7E printable ASCII | unchanged | unchanged |
| **ALL non-ASCII ≥ U+0080** (incl. printable ones: C1 controls U+0080–U+009F, `©`, `é`, `中`, `😀`, combining U+0301, U+200B, U+2028, U+2029, U+FEFF, U+00A0, even U+00B7 itself) | literal ASCII text `\u{<hex>}` — backslash `u` `{` lowercase-hex-no-leading-zeros `}` | same `\u{...}` form |

Exact probe: input bytes 0x00–0x1F + 0x7F (`ctrl.bin`):
- unicode: `␀␁␂␃␄␅␆␇␈├─┤␊\n␋␌␍␎␏␐␑␒␓␔␕␖␗␘␙␚␛␜␝␞␟␡`
  (hex: `e2 90 80` … `e2 90 88`, then `e2 94 9c e2 94 80 e2 94 a4` (├─┤), `e2 90 8a 0a`, …, `e2 90 a1`; exit 0)
- caret: `^@^A^B^C^D^E^F^G^H├─┤^J\n^K^L^M^N^O^P^Q^R^S^T^U^V^W^X^Y^Z^[^\^]^^^_^?`
  (tab still rendered as box-drawing placeholder `├─┤` even in caret mode)

Note: NUL bytes normally trigger binary detection, but `-A` overrides it (help: "This option
can also be used to print binary files"). `printf 'hello\x00world\n' | -A` →
`hello␀world␊\n` (hex `68 65 6c 6c 6f e2 90 80 77 6f 72 6c 64 e2 90 8a 0a`), exit 0.

More vectors:
- `X U+200B Y U+2028 Z U+00A9 W U+2029 V U+0301 U+0301 \n` →
  `X\u{200b}Y\u{2028}Z\u{a9}W\u{2029}V\u{301}\u{301}␊\n`
- `a b©é中😀 U+0301 \x7f €\n` → `a·b\u{a9}\u{e9}\u{4e2d}\u{1f600}\u{301}␡\u{20ac}␊\n`
- CRLF `a b\r\nc\rd\n` → `a·b␍␊\nc␍d␊\n` (caret: `a·b^M^J\nc^Md^J\n`). Lone CR is NOT a line break.
- Input ESC (0x1B) e.g. `\e[31mRED\e[0m ...` → `␛[31mRED␛[0m·normal·...` (ESC→␊-style glyph U+241B ␛, the `[31m` chars are ordinary printable).
- File without trailing newline: no glyph and no newline appended: `nonl` (no `\n`) → `nonl`.
- **BOM is NOT stripped under `-A`**: file `EF BB BF hello\n` → `\u{feff}hello␊\n`
  (contrast: ANSI path strips BOM, §8).

### 1.2 Colors of `-A` glyphs (ANSI path, default theme = auto-dark)

Measured with `-A -f --style=plain` (or `--color=always`), default theme. Each glyph class
is emitted as its own `\e[38;5;<n>m … \e[0m` segment:

- normal text: `38;5;231` (theme fg)
- tab placeholder `├─┤` / `↹`: `38;5;141`
- LF glyph `␊`: `38;5;203`; CR glyph `␍`: `38;5;186`
- space glyph `·`: `38;5;81`
- `\u{...}` escapes: `38;5;242`
- C0/DEL glyphs (`␀`…`␟`, `␡`) and caret sequences (`^A`, `^?`, `^J`): **no special color —
  inherit the surrounding text segment's color** (they are spliced into the text run).

Example `a\tb\n` with `-A -f`:
```
\e[38;5;231ma\e[0m\e[38;5;141m├─┤\e[0m\e[38;5;231mb\e[0m\e[38;5;203m␊\e[0m\n
```
Example `a\x01\x7f\xC2\x80z\n` (unicode notation):
```
\e[38;5;231ma␁␡\e[0m\e[38;5;242m\u{80}\e[0m\e[38;5;231mz\e[0m\e[38;5;203m␊\e[0m
```
caret notation same input:
```
\e[38;5;231ma^A^?\e[0m\e[38;5;242m\u{80}\e[0m\e[38;5;231mz^J\e[0m
```
These colors are **theme-dependent**: with `--theme=TwoDark` text is 249, `\u{..}` is 241,
`␊` inherits text color; with `--theme=base16` text is `\e[37m`, `\u{..}` is `38;5;8`.
(Tab/newline/space glyph colors per theme were only fully measured for the default theme.)

### 1.3 `-A` interactions

- `-A` works fully in piped plain mode (no colors/decorations): glyphs uncolored, e.g.
  `x y\n` → `x·y␊\n` (hex `78 c2 b7 79 e2 90 8a 0a`).
- With decorations: `-A --decorations=always` shows normal grid/numbers; content replaced.
  Tab placeholder width is computed from the content column with default tab width 4.
- `-A` + `--wrap`: wrapping applies to the *replaced* text (glyphs count as width 1 each,
  placeholder counts its display width).

## 2. `--tabs N` and tab expansion

### 2.1 When expansion happens

| Mode | default (no `--tabs`) | `--tabs N` (N>0) | `--tabs 0` |
|---|---|---|---|
| plain piped (path 1) | raw `\t` passthrough | raw `\t` passthrough (**ignored**) | raw `\t` |
| `--color=always --style=plain` | **raw `\t` kept** (inside a colored segment) | expanded to spaces | raw `\t` |
| decorations on (with or without color) | expanded to spaces, **width 4** | expanded to spaces, width N | raw `\t` |
| `-A` (any mode) | placeholder, width 4 | placeholder, width N | placeholder, **width 4** (0 ignored under -A) |

Examples (content `abc\td\n`, tx1):
- piped plain, `--tabs 4`: `61 62 63 09 64 0a` (unchanged)
- `--color=always --style=plain`, no `--tabs`: `\e[38;5;231mabc\td\e[0m\n` (09 kept)
- same with `--tabs 4`: `\e[38;5;231mabc    d\e[0m\n` (4 spaces)
- `--decorations=always`, no `--tabs`, content line: `   1 │ abc d` (1 space: col 3→4)
- syntax-highlighted python (`\treturn 1`), color, no `--tabs`: 09 kept in its own 231 segment;
  with `--tabs 4`: 4 spaces, same 231 segment. Expanded spaces take the color of the
  surrounding token segment.

### 2.2 Expansion rule (spaces)

Tab at 0-based display column `c` with width `N` → `N - (c mod N)` spaces
(verified N=1,2,3,4,8 at various columns). `--tabs 999` accepted.

### 2.3 `-A` placeholder rule

Tab placeholder display width `w = N - (c mod N)` (default N=4, also when `--tabs 0`):
- `w == 1` → `↹` (U+21B9, bytes `e2 86 b9`)
- `w == 2` → `├┤`
- `w >= 3` → `├` + `─`×(w−2) + `┤`
(`├`=e2 94 9c, `─`=e2 94 80, `┤`=e2 94 a4)

Vectors: `a\tb` default N=4 → `a├─┤b` (w=3); N=8 → `a├─────┤b` (w=7);
`ab\tc` N=2 → `ab├┤c`; N=3 → `ab↹c`; `abc\td` N=0 → `abc↹d` (falls back to 4);
`abcd\te` N=0 → `abcd├──┤e` (w=4).

### 2.4 Errors

`--tabs -1` → clap error (parsed as flag), exit 2:
```
error: unexpected argument '-1' found

  tip: to pass '-1' as a value, use '-- -1'

Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]...
       executable <COMMAND>
```

## 3. `--wrap` and `--terminal-width`

### 3.1 Activation

- Plain piped path: **never wraps**, regardless of `--wrap`/`--terminal-width`.
- Color or decorations active: wraps at `min(terminal_width)`; content area width =
  terminal width − sidebar width (with default numbers+grid style the sidebar is
  `␣␣␣N␣│␣` = 7 columns: 4-wide right-aligned number, space, `│`, space).
- `--wrap` values: `auto` (default), `never`, `character`, `word`.
- `auto` behaves exactly like `character` in all piped tests (with color and/or decorations).
- `never` = no wrapping, lines printed in full (no truncation despite `-S` docs saying
  "Truncate"; `-S/--chop-long-lines` is an alias for `--wrap=never` and does NOT truncate).

### 3.2 character wrap

Breaks at exactly the content width. With `--color=always --style=plain --terminal-width 10`:
`aaaa bbbb cccc dddd eeee ffff gggg hhhh\n` → 4 lines of 10 chars:
`aaaa bbbb ` / `cccc dddd ` / `eeee ffff ` / `gggg hhhh`. Each wrapped output line is
`\e[38;5;231m<10 chars>\e[0m\n` (color closed and reopened per output line).

With decorations (`--terminal-width 20`, content width 13):
```
   1 │ aaaa bbbb ccc
     │ c dddd eeee f
     │ fff gggg hhhh
```
Continuation lines get the sidebar with a **blank number field** (5 spaces + `│` + space).
The header `File: wrap.txt` is also character-wrapped into the same content width
(`File: wrap.tx` / `t` at width 20; `File: w` / `rap.txt` at width 14).

### 3.3 word wrap

Greedy break at spaces; a word longer than the width is character-split (no hyphen
awareness: `aaaa-bbbb` at width 6 → `aaaa-b` / `bbb`; `cccc_dddd` → `cccc_d`/`ddd`;
`ee/ff` (5) stayed whole at width 6). Continuation lines are NOT indented (start at
content column 0) — leading indent of the source line is not carried over:
`    aaaa bbbb cccc dddd eeee` at width 12 → `    aaaa` / `bbbb cccc` / `dddd eeee`.

Width-20 vectors (content 13): `aaaa bbbb` / `cccc dddd` / `eeee ffff` / `gggg hhhh`
(single separating space dropped at the break).

Edge-case vectors (all `--color=always --style=plain`, width = terminal width since plain style):
- `aa bb cc` w=4 → `aa`/`bb`/`cc`; w=5 → `aa bb` / `␣cc` (leading space kept!)
- `aa  bb` (two spaces) w=4 → `aa␣` / `bb`; w=5 → `aa␣` / `bb`
- `aaa bb` w=4 → `aaa`/`bb`; w=5 → `aaa`/`bb` (space dropped)
- `a  b   c d` w=6 → `a  b  ` / ` c d` (word mode == char mode here)
- 36×`a` at content width 5 → 7 lines of `aaaaa` + `a`
- header word-wrap quirk at width 12: `File: longword.txt` → `File:` / `␣long` / `word.` / `txt`
  (leading space kept on continuation — differs from content wrapping at other widths)

The exact word-wrap algorithm could not be fully inferred from these probes (trailing/leading
space handling at the break is inconsistent between cases); treat the above as golden vectors.

### 3.4 Width counting

- CJK wide chars count 2 columns: `你好世界abc你好` at width 10 → `你好世界ab` (10 cols) / `c你好`.
- Combining chars (e+U+0301) count 0 and never separate from their base char.
- Input ANSI escape sequences count 0 width (wrapping measured on visible chars only).
- Tabs (when expanded) count their expanded width.

### 3.5 Terminal width resolution

- Default (piped, no env): 80.
- `--terminal-width N`: N. `+N`/`-N`: offset from the "actual" width (piped actual = 80):
  `--terminal-width +70` → 150, `-70` → 10 (grid widths measured).
- `BAT_WIDTH` env: same semantics as `--terminal-width` (BAT_WIDTH=30 → width 30).
- `COLUMNS` is ignored.
- Errors (clap, exit 2): `--terminal-width 0` →
  `error: invalid value '0' for '--terminal-width <width>': terminal width cannot be zero`;
  `BAT_WIDTH=abc` →
  `error: invalid value 'abc' for '--terminal-width <width>': must be an offset or number`.

### 3.6 ANSI in input + wrapping (color path, strip-ansi=never)

Input `\e[31mRED\e[0m normal text here ok\n`, width 12, character wrap, plain style:
```
\e[31m\e[38;5;231m\e[31mRED\e[0m\e[0m\e[38;5;231m normal t\e[0m\n
\e[38;5;231mext here ok\e[0m\n
```
i.e. the input escape is re-emitted, then bat's own color, then the input escape again
before the covered text; input sequences do not count toward width.

## 4. `-r/--line-range`

### 4.1 Syntax and semantics (1-based, inclusive, original file numbering)

Test file: `seq 1 20`. All exit 0 unless noted.

| arg | result |
|---|---|
| `5` | `5` |
| `5:8` | `5 6 7 8` |
| `5:` | 5..20 |
| `:8` | 1..8 |
| `5:+3` | `5 6 7 8` (N..N+M) |
| `1:+0` | `1` |
| `+3` | `3` (leading `+` accepted, like bare N) |
| `-3:` | `18 19 20` (last 3 lines; negative N allowed for `-r`) |
| `8::3` | 5..11 (line 8 with 3 context each side) |
| `5:8:2` | 3..10 (range 5-8 plus 2 context each side) |
| `18::10` | 8..20 (clamped at EOF) |
| `15:30` | 15..20 (clamped) |
| `30:40` | (empty output, exit 0) |
| `8:5` | (empty, exit 0) |
| `0` | (empty, exit 0) |
| `0:3` | `1 2 3` (0 clamps to 1) |
| multiple `-r 2:3 -r 5:6` | `2 3 5 6` |
| overlapping `-r 2:5 -r 4:7` | `2 3 4 5 6 7` (merged, no duplicates) |

- Applies per file when multiple files given (`-r 2 plain.txt nums.txt` → `world`, `2`).
- Line numbers shown are the ORIGINAL file line numbers (`--style=numbers` showed 2,3,5,6).
- With grid/snip style, disjoint ranges are separated by a snip line (see 4.3).
- With decorations, an out-of-range selection still prints header+grid, empty body, exit 0.

### 4.2 Errors (stderr, exit 1; message always colored `\e[31m…\e[0m` even when piped)

- `-r abc` / `-r '::'` → `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: invalid digit found in string\n`
- `-r ':'` → `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: cannot parse integer from empty string\n`
- `-r '1:2:3:4'` → `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: Line range contained too many ':' characters. Expected format: 'N', 'N:M', 'N::C', or 'N:M:C'\n`
- `-r ' 3'` (leading space) → `invalid digit found in string` (no trimming)

### 4.3 Snip line (grid style, between disjoint ranges)

Width 80: ` ... │ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ 8< ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─\n`
(number field = right-aligned `...` in 4 chars + ` │ `; content = 35 `─` and 35 spaces
interleaved as `─ `×18? — exact repr: `'─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ 8< ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─'`,
i.e. 18 dashes space-separated, ` 8< `, 17 more space-separated dashes; total content width 72).
Width 20: `' ... │ ─ ─ ─ 8< ─ ─\n'` (content = `─ ─ ─ 8< ─ ─`, 12 chars).
Snip line only appears when the `snip` style component AND grid are active
(default style includes snip; `--style=numbers` alone shows no separator).

## 5. `-H/--highlight-line`

- Same range syntax as `-r` (`40`, `30:40`, `:40`, `40:`, `30:+10` verified) **except**
  negative ranges: `-H '-2:'` → clap error `error: unexpected argument '-2' found` (exit 2),
  while `-r '-2:'` works. Quirk confirmed.
- No effect on the plain piped path.
- Highlighted line: content segments get background prepended per segment:
  `\e[48;5;236;38;5;<fg>m<text>\e[0m` (bg `48;5;236` in both default theme and TwoDark;
  fg is the token's normal color). After the content, the rest of the line is padded with
  spaces in `\e[48;5;236m<spaces>\e[0m` up to the full terminal width (or content-area width
  when a sidebar is present). `\n` after.
- With grid+numbers: the line-number field and `│` separator are NOT highlighted
  (stay `38;5;246`); the space after `│` is not highlighted; content+padding are.
  Width 20: `   2 │ ` then `\e[48;5;236;38;5;231m2\e[0m\e[48;5;236m` + 12 spaces + `\e[0m\n`.
- Empty highlighted line: `\e[48;5;236m` + full-width spaces + `\e[0m\n` (no content segment).
- Wrapped highlighted line: every continuation line gets the bg; only the last (short)
  continuation gets bg padding.
- `-r` and `-H` compose: `-r 5 -H 5` highlights the printed line (original numbering).
- Out-of-range `-H 99`: silently ignored. Invalid `-H abc` →
  `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: invalid digit found in string\n` on stderr, exit 1.

## 6. `-s/--squeeze-blank` and `--squeeze-limit`

- `-s`/`--squeeze-blank`: collapses runs of TRULY EMPTY lines (zero chars before `\n`) to one.
  `a\n\n\n\n\nb\n\n\nc\n` → `a\n\nb\n\nc\n`. Works even on the plain piped path.
- Lines containing only whitespace are NOT blank: `a\n   \n\t\nb\n` unchanged under `-s`.
- `--squeeze-limit N` alone (without `-s`) does nothing (verified N=0,2).
- `-s --squeeze-limit 0`: removes ALL empty lines → `a\nb\nc\n`.
- `-s --squeeze-limit 2`: keeps at most 2 → `a\n\n\nb\n\n\nc\n`.
- Line numbers keep original values when squeezing (`1 a`, `2 ␣`, `6 b`, `7 ␣`, `9 c`).
- `--squeeze-limit -1` → clap `unexpected argument '-1'` error, exit 2.

## 7. `--strip-ansi <when>`

Values `auto`, `always`, `never` (default `never`); invalid value → clap error exit 2.
Only effective on the transforming paths (color/decorations); plain piped path always passes
input ANSI through untouched.

- `never` (default): input escape sequences are kept (see 3.6 for how they are re-emitted
  when coloring). With a real syntax (`-l py`), the raw ESC bytes get tokenized as text and
  re-emitted (messy but preserved).
- `always`: input ANSI stripped before highlighting, even for plain text:
  `\e[31mRED\e[0m normal…` → `\e[38;5;231mRED normal text here ok\e[0m\n`.
- `auto`: strips unless the detected syntax is plain text (auto-detected `.txt` or `-l txt`
  keeps the input ANSI; `-l py` strips).

## 8. Binary, encodings, edge inputs

### 8.1 Binary detection

- A file is "binary" if a NUL (0x00) occurs within the **first 1024 bytes** (offsets 0–1023).
  Verified boundary: NUL at offset 1023 → binary; offset 1024 → not binary.
- UTF-16 files WITH a BOM (FF FE or FE FF) are NOT binary — they are transcoded to UTF-8
  on the transforming paths: `FF FE 68 00 69 00` → `\e[38;5;231mhi\e[0m` (NULs gone,
  no trailing newline added). UTF-16 without BOM → NULs in first 1024 → binary.
- Default `--binary=no-printing` behavior:
  - plain piped path: content printed RAW anyway (NULs included), no warning, exit 0.
    (`hello\x00world\n` → `hello\0world\n`)
  - color path: content suppressed; this warning goes to **stdout** (not stderr!), exit 0:
    `\e[33m[bat warning]\e[0m: Binary content from file 'nul.bin' will not be printed to the terminal (but will be present if the output of 'bat' is piped). You can use 'bat -A' to show the binary file contents.\n`
    For stdin: `… Binary content from STDIN will not be printed …`.
  - decorations path: header line becomes `     │ File: nul.bin   <BINARY>` (3 spaces before
    `<BINARY>`), no content lines, no warning, exit 0.
- `--binary=as-text`: content printed normally everywhere (NULs raw; with decorations the
  NUL passes through into the content line: `   1 │ hello\0world`).
- `-A`: prints binary with the glyph mapping (§1).

### 8.2 Invalid UTF-8

- Plain piped: raw passthrough (`bad \xff\xfe utf8\n` unchanged), exit 0.
- Color path: each invalid byte replaced with U+FFFD (`ef bf bd`), inside the text segment:
  `\e[38;5;231mbad ��� utf8\e[0m\n` (here `��` = 2×U+FFFD), exit 0, no error/warning.

### 8.3 BOM (UTF-8)

- Plain piped: BOM `ef bb bf` passed through.
- Color path: BOM stripped: file `EF BB BF hello\n` → `\e[38;5;231mhello\e[0m\n`.
- `-A`: BOM NOT stripped, shown as `\u{feff}` (see 1.1).

### 8.4 CRLF / lone CR

- Plain piped: `\r\n` passed through raw.
- Color path: line content `line1\r\n` → `\e[38;5;231mline1\e[0m\r\n` — the `\r` is preserved
  but emitted AFTER the `\e[0m`, immediately before `\n`. Mid-line `\r` stays inside the
  colored segment (`a\rb\n` → `\e[38;5;231ma\rb\e[0m\n`). Lines split on `\n` only.

### 8.5 Missing trailing newline

- Plain piped and color path: nothing added — output ends without `\n`
  (`nonl` → `nonl`, color: `\e[38;5;231mnonl\e[0m`).
- Decorations path: a `\n` IS added after the last content line
  (`   1 │ nonl\n` then the bottom grid line).
- `-A`: no `␊` glyph and no `\n` added for the final unterminated line.

### 8.6 Empty input

- Plain piped: zero output, exit 0.
- Decorations: header `     │ File: empty.txt   <EMPTY>` (or `     │ STDIN   <EMPTY>` for
  stdin), top+bottom grid, no content, exit 0.
- `-E/--quiet-empty`: empty input → absolutely no output (not even header), exit 0.

### 8.7 Long lines

1 000 000-char line: printed in full (plain: 1000001 bytes; color+wrap=never: 1000016 =
+15 bytes for the two ANSI sequences). No truncation or performance cutoffs observed.

## 9. Errors & exit codes summary

- clap/usage errors (bad enum value, bad `--terminal-width`, `-1` flags, `-H '-2:'`):
  plain `error: …` text on stderr, exit **2**.
- runtime bat errors (bad `-r`/`-H` range strings): stderr
  `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: <msg>\n` (colored even when piped), exit **1**.
- binary/empty/invalid-UTF-8/out-of-range: all exit **0**.

## 10. Notable golden vectors for testing

```
printf 'a\tb\n'               -A                       → a├─┤b␊\n
printf 'a\tb\n'               -A --tabs 8              → a├─────┤b␊\n
printf 'ab\tc\n'              -A --tabs 3              → ab↹c␊\n
printf 'x y\n'                -A                       → x·y␊\n
bytes 00..1F,7F               -A --nonprintable-notation=caret → ^@^A..^H├─┤^J\n^K..^M..^_^?
'©é中😀'                       -A                       → \u{a9}\u{e9}\u{4e2d}\u{1f600}
printf 'hello\x00world\n'     (piped plain)            → raw bytes incl. \0, exit 0
printf 'hello\x00world\n'     --color=always --style=plain → \e[33m[bat warning]\e[0m: Binary content from file '…' will not be printed… (stdout!), exit 0
printf '\xef\xbb\xbfhi\n'     --color=always --style=plain → \e[38;5;231mhi\e[0m\n   (BOM stripped)
printf 'l1\r\nl2\r\n'         --color=always --style=plain → \e[38;5;231ml1\e[0m\r\n\e[38;5;231ml2\e[0m\r\n
printf 'nonl'                 --color=always --style=plain → \e[38;5;231mnonl\e[0m   (no \n added)
printf 'nonl'                 --decorations=always     → content line gets \n added
seq 1 20 | -r 5:8:2           → 3..10
seq 1 20 | -r 2:3 -r 5:6 + grid → snip line ' ... │ ─ … 8< … ─'
-H 2 --terminal-width 20 --style=plain --color=always on '2\n':
  \e[48;5;236;38;5;231m2\e[0m\e[48;5;236m<19 spaces>\e[0m\n
```

display.content:
# Spec: Content transformations (bat 0.26.1, binary `610b77c`)

Recon area: `-A/--show-all`, `--nonprintable-notation`, `--tabs`, `--wrap`, `-r/--line-range`,
`-H/--highlight-line`, `-s/--squeeze-blank`/`--squeeze-limit`, `--strip-ansi`, binary handling,
encodings (invalid UTF-8, BOM, UTF-16, CRLF), missing trailing newline, empty input, long lines.

All probes used a scrubbed environment unless noted:

```
env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=/tmp/fakehome TERM=xterm ./executable <args>
```

stdout was a pipe in all probes (the judge's normal mode). `--paging=never` was passed for safety
(paging never engages when stdout is not a tty anyway).

## 0. The three output paths (fundamental)

Behavior depends on which of three paths is taken:

1. **Plain passthrough path** — stdout piped AND no `--color=always`/`-f` AND no
   `--decorations=always` (default piped style is plain) AND no `-A`:
   the input bytes are copied **byte-for-byte** to stdout. In this mode ALL of
   `--tabs`, `--wrap`, `--terminal-width`, `--strip-ansi`, `--binary`, invalid-UTF-8
   replacement and BOM stripping are **ignored**. `-s/--squeeze-blank` and `-r/--line-range`
   **do** still apply in this mode.
2. **ANSI printer path** — `--color=always` (or tty): content re-emitted with ANSI styles,
   wrapping, tab expansion, UTF-8 sanitizing, BOM handling, binary suppression all active.
3. **Decorations path** — `--decorations=always` (or tty): grid/numbers/header printed;
   content transformation active even without color.

`-A` forces a transforming printer path even when piped plain (but does not add
decorations or colors by itself).

Default when piped: style = plain, color = off → path 1. Verified:
`printf 'hello\nworld\n' > plain.txt; ./executable plain.txt` → stdout `hello\nworld\n`, exit 0.

Default terminal width when piped (no COLUMNS/BAT_WIDTH honored): **80**.
`COLUMNS=30` had no effect; `BAT_WIDTH=30` did (grid became 30 wide).

## 1. `-A/--show-all` and `--nonprintable-notation`

Long flag `--show-all` confirmed working. `--nonprintable-notation` accepts only
`unicode` (default) and `caret`; any other value → clap error, exit 2:

```
error: invalid value 'foo' for '--nonprintable-notation <notation>'
  [possible values: unicode, caret]
```

### 1.1 Replacement mapping (both notations unless noted)

Input is treated as raw bytes/UTF-8; replacement is per character:

| Input | unicode notation | caret notation |
|---|---|---|
| 0x00–0x08, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x0E–0x1F (C0 except \t,\n,\r) | U+2400+codepoint (␀…␟), single glyph | `^@`…`^_` (caret + codepoint+0x40), 2 ASCII chars |
| 0x09 TAB | tab placeholder (see §2): `├`+`─`*n+`┤`, or `↹` (U+21B9) if width 1 | same as unicode |
| 0x0A LF | `␊` (U+240A) followed by real `\n` | `^J` followed by real `\n` |
| 0x0D CR | `␍` (U+240D), inline (no line break) | `^M` |
| 0x20 SPACE | `·` (U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT) | `·` (same) |
| 0x7F DEL | `␡` (U+2421) | `^?` |
| 0x21–0x7E printable ASCII | unchanged | unchanged |
| **ALL non-ASCII ≥ U+0080** (incl. printable ones: C1 controls U+0080–U+009F, `©`, `é`, `中`, `😀`, combining U+0301, U+200B, U+2028, U+2029, U+FEFF, U+00A0, even U+00B7 itself) | literal ASCII text `\u{<hex>}` — backslash `u` `{` lowercase-hex-no-leading-zeros `}` | same `\u{...}` form |

Exact probe: input bytes 0x00–0x1F + 0x7F (`ctrl.bin`):
- unicode: `␀␁␂␃␄␅␆␇␈├─┤␊\n␋␌␍␎␏␐␑␒␓␔␕␖␗␘␙␚␛␜␝␞␟␡`
  (hex: `e2 90 80` … `e2 90 88`, then `e2 94 9c e2 94 80 e2 94 a4` (├─┤), `e2 90 8a 0a`, …, `e2 90 a1`; exit 0)
- caret: `^@^A^B^C^D^E^F^G^H├─┤^J\n^K^L^M^N^O^P^Q^R^S^T^U^V^W^X^Y^Z^[^\^]^^^_^?`
  (tab still rendered as box-drawing placeholder `├─┤` even in caret mode)

Note: NUL bytes normally trigger binary detection, but `-A` overrides it (help: "This option
can also be used to print binary files"). `printf 'hello\x00world\n' | -A` →
`hello␀world␊\n` (hex `68 65 6c 6c 6f e2 90 80 77 6f 72 6c 64 e2 90 8a 0a`), exit 0.

More vectors:
- `X U+200B Y U+2028 Z U+00A9 W U+2029 V U+0301 U+0301 \n` →
  `X\u{200b}Y\u{2028}Z\u{a9}W\u{2029}V\u{301}\u{301}␊\n`
- `a b©é中😀 U+0301 \x7f €\n` → `a·b\u{a9}\u{e9}\u{4e2d}\u{1f600}\u{301}␡\u{20ac}␊\n`
- CRLF `a b\r\nc\rd\n` → `a·b␍␊\nc␍d␊\n` (caret: `a·b^M^J\nc^Md^J\n`). Lone CR is NOT a line break.
- Input ESC (0x1B) e.g. `\e[31mRED\e[0m ...` → `␛[31mRED␛[0m·normal·...` (ESC→␊-style glyph U+241B ␛, the `[31m` chars are ordinary printable).
- File without trailing newline: no glyph and no newline appended: `nonl` (no `\n`) → `nonl`.
- **BOM is NOT stripped under `-A`**: file `EF BB BF hello\n` → `\u{feff}hello␊\n`
  (contrast: ANSI path strips BOM, §8).

### 1.2 Colors of `-A` glyphs (ANSI path, default theme = auto-dark)

Measured with `-A -f --style=plain` (or `--color=always`), default theme. Each glyph class
is emitted as its own `\e[38;5;<n>m … \e[0m` segment:

- normal text: `38;5;231` (theme fg)
- tab placeholder `├─┤` / `↹`: `38;5;141`
- LF glyph `␊`: `38;5;203`; CR glyph `␍`: `38;5;186`
- space glyph `·`: `38;5;81`
- `\u{...}` escapes: `38;5;242`
- C0/DEL glyphs (`␀`…`␟`, `␡`) and caret sequences (`^A`, `^?`, `^J`): **no special color —
  inherit the surrounding text segment's color** (they are spliced into the text run).

Example `a\tb\n` with `-A -f`:
```
\e[38;5;231ma\e[0m\e[38;5;141m├─┤\e[0m\e[38;5;231mb\e[0m\e[38;5;203m␊\e[0m\n
```
Example `a\x01\x7f\xC2\x80z\n` (unicode notation):
```
\e[38;5;231ma␁␡\e[0m\e[38;5;242m\u{80}\e[0m\e[38;5;231mz\e[0m\e[38;5;203m␊\e[0m
```
caret notation same input:
```
\e[38;5;231ma^A^?\e[0m\e[38;5;242m\u{80}\e[0m\e[38;5;231mz^J\e[0m
```
These colors are **theme-dependent**: with `--theme=TwoDark` text is 249, `\u{..}` is 241,
`␊` inherits text color; with `--theme=base16` text is `\e[37m`, `\u{..}` is `38;5;8`.
(Tab/newline/space glyph colors per theme were only fully measured for the default theme.)

### 1.3 `-A` interactions

- `-A` works fully in piped plain mode (no colors/decorations): glyphs uncolored, e.g.
  `x y\n` → `x·y␊\n` (hex `78 c2 b7 79 e2 90 8a 0a`).
- With decorations: `-A --decorations=always` shows normal grid/numbers; content replaced.
  Tab placeholder width is computed from the content column with default tab width 4.
- `-A` + `--wrap`: wrapping applies to the *replaced* text (glyphs count as width 1 each,
  placeholder counts its display width).

## 2. `--tabs N` and tab expansion

### 2.1 When expansion happens

| Mode | default (no `--tabs`) | `--tabs N` (N>0) | `--tabs 0` |
|---|---|---|---|
| plain piped (path 1) | raw `\t` passthrough | raw `\t` passthrough (**ignored**) | raw `\t` |
| `--color=always --style=plain` | **raw `\t` kept** (inside a colored segment) | expanded to spaces | raw `\t` |
| decorations on (with or without color) | expanded to spaces, **width 4** | expanded to spaces, width N | raw `\t` |
| `-A` (any mode) | placeholder, width 4 | placeholder, width N | placeholder, **width 4** (0 ignored under -A) |

Examples (content `abc\td\n`, tx1):
- piped plain, `--tabs 4`: `61 62 63 09 64 0a` (unchanged)
- `--color=always --style=plain`, no `--tabs`: `\e[38;5;231mabc\td\e[0m\n` (09 kept)
- same with `--tabs 4`: `\e[38;5;231mabc    d\e[0m\n` (4 spaces)
- `--decorations=always`, no `--tabs`, content line: `   1 │ abc d` (1 space: col 3→4)
- syntax-highlighted python (`\treturn 1`), color, no `--tabs`: 09 kept in its own 231 segment;
  with `--tabs 4`: 4 spaces, same 231 segment. Expanded spaces take the color of the
  surrounding token segment.

### 2.2 Expansion rule (spaces)

Tab at 0-based display column `c` with width `N` → `N - (c mod N)` spaces
(verified N=1,2,3,4,8 at various columns). `--tabs 999` accepted.

### 2.3 `-A` placeholder rule

Tab placeholder display width `w = N - (c mod N)` (default N=4, also when `--tabs 0`):
- `w == 1` → `↹` (U+21B9, bytes `e2 86 b9`)
- `w == 2` → `├┤`
- `w >= 3` → `├` + `─`×(w−2) + `┤`
(`├`=e2 94 9c, `─`=e2 94 80, `┤`=e2 94 a4)

Vectors: `a\tb` default N=4 → `a├─┤b` (w=3); N=8 → `a├─────┤b` (w=7);
`ab\tc` N=2 → `ab├┤c`; N=3 → `ab↹c`; `abc\td` N=0 → `abc↹d` (falls back to 4);
`abcd\te` N=0 → `abcd├──┤e` (w=4).

### 2.4 Errors

`--tabs -1` → clap error (parsed as flag), exit 2:
```
error: unexpected argument '-1' found

  tip: to pass '-1' as a value, use '-- -1'

Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]...
       executable <COMMAND>
```

## 3. `--wrap` and `--terminal-width`

### 3.1 Activation

- Plain piped path: **never wraps**, regardless of `--wrap`/`--terminal-width`.
- Color or decorations active: wraps at `min(terminal_width)`; content area width =
  terminal width − sidebar width (with default numbers+grid style the sidebar is
  `␣␣␣N␣│␣` = 7 columns: 4-wide right-aligned number, space, `│`, space).
- `--wrap` values: `auto` (default), `never`, `character`, `word`.
- `auto` behaves exactly like `character` in all piped tests (with color and/or decorations).
- `never` = no wrapping, lines printed in full (no truncation despite `-S` docs saying
  "Truncate"; `-S/--chop-long-lines` is an alias for `--wrap=never` and does NOT truncate).

### 3.2 character wrap

Breaks at exactly the content width. With `--color=always --style=plain --terminal-width 10`:
`aaaa bbbb cccc dddd eeee ffff gggg hhhh\n` → 4 lines of 10 chars:
`aaaa bbbb ` / `cccc dddd ` / `eeee ffff ` / `gggg hhhh`. Each wrapped output line is
`\e[38;5;231m<10 chars>\e[0m\n` (color closed and reopened per output line).

With decorations (`--terminal-width 20`, content width 13):
```
   1 │ aaaa bbbb ccc
     │ c dddd eeee f
     │ fff gggg hhhh
```
Continuation lines get the sidebar with a **blank number field** (5 spaces + `│` + space).
The header `File: wrap.txt` is also character-wrapped into the same content width
(`File: wrap.tx` / `t` at width 20; `File: w` / `rap.txt` at width 14).

### 3.3 word wrap

Greedy break at spaces; a word longer than the width is character-split (no hyphen
awareness: `aaaa-bbbb` at width 6 → `aaaa-b` / `bbb`; `cccc_dddd` → `cccc_d`/`ddd`;
`ee/ff` (5) stayed whole at width 6). Continuation lines are NOT indented (start at
content column 0) — leading indent of the source line is not carried over:
`    aaaa bbbb cccc dddd eeee` at width 12 → `    aaaa` / `bbbb cccc` / `dddd eeee`.

Width-20 vectors (content 13): `aaaa bbbb` / `cccc dddd` / `eeee ffff` / `gggg hhhh`
(single separating space dropped at the break).

Edge-case vectors (all `--color=always --style=plain`, width = terminal width since plain style):
- `aa bb cc` w=4 → `aa`/`bb`/`cc`; w=5 → `aa bb` / `␣cc` (leading space kept!)
- `aa  bb` (two spaces) w=4 → `aa␣` / `bb`; w=5 → `aa␣` / `bb`
- `aaa bb` w=4 → `aaa`/`bb`; w=5 → `aaa`/`bb` (space dropped)
- `a  b   c d` w=6 → `a  b  ` / ` c d` (word mode == char mode here)
- 36×`a` at content width 5 → 7 lines of `aaaaa` + `a`
- header word-wrap quirk at width 12: `File: longword.txt` → `File:` / `␣long` / `word.` / `txt`
  (leading space kept on continuation — differs from content wrapping at other widths)

The exact word-wrap algorithm could not be fully inferred from these probes (trailing/leading
space handling at the break is inconsistent between cases); treat the above as golden vectors.

### 3.4 Width counting

- CJK wide chars count 2 columns: `你好世界abc你好` at width 10 → `你好世界ab` (10 cols) / `c你好`.
- Combining chars (e+U+0301) count 0 and never separate from their base char.
- Input ANSI escape sequences count 0 width (wrapping measured on visible chars only).
- Tabs (when expanded) count their expanded width.

### 3.5 Terminal width resolution

- Default (piped, no env): 80.
- `--terminal-width N`: N. `+N`/`-N`: offset from the "actual" width (piped actual = 80):
  `--terminal-width +70` → 150, `-70` → 10 (grid widths measured).
- `BAT_WIDTH` env: same semantics as `--terminal-width` (BAT_WIDTH=30 → width 30).
- `COLUMNS` is ignored.
- Errors (clap, exit 2): `--terminal-width 0` →
  `error: invalid value '0' for '--terminal-width <width>': terminal width cannot be zero`;
  `BAT_WIDTH=abc` →
  `error: invalid value 'abc' for '--terminal-width <width>': must be an offset or number`.

### 3.6 ANSI in input + wrapping (color path, strip-ansi=never)

Input `\e[31mRED\e[0m normal text here ok\n`, width 12, character wrap, plain style:
```
\e[31m\e[38;5;231m\e[31mRED\e[0m\e[0m\e[38;5;231m normal t\e[0m\n
\e[38;5;231mext here ok\e[0m\n
```
i.e. the input escape is re-emitted, then bat's own color, then the input escape again
before the covered text; input sequences do not count toward width.

## 4. `-r/--line-range`

### 4.1 Syntax and semantics (1-based, inclusive, original file numbering)

Test file: `seq 1 20`. All exit 0 unless noted.

| arg | result |
|---|---|
| `5` | `5` |
| `5:8` | `5 6 7 8` |
| `5:` | 5..20 |
| `:8` | 1..8 |
| `5:+3` | `5 6 7 8` (N..N+M) |
| `1:+0` | `1` |
| `+3` | `3` (leading `+` accepted, like bare N) |
| `-3:` | `18 19 20` (last 3 lines; negative N allowed for `-r`) |
| `8::3` | 5..11 (line 8 with 3 context each side) |
| `5:8:2` | 3..10 (range 5-8 plus 2 context each side) |
| `18::10` | 8..20 (clamped at EOF) |
| `15:30` | 15..20 (clamped) |
| `30:40` | (empty output, exit 0) |
| `8:5` | (empty, exit 0) |
| `0` | (empty, exit 0) |
| `0:3` | `1 2 3` (0 clamps to 1) |
| multiple `-r 2:3 -r 5:6` | `2 3 5 6` |
| overlapping `-r 2:5 -r 4:7` | `2 3 4 5 6 7` (merged, no duplicates) |

- Applies per file when multiple files given (`-r 2 plain.txt nums.txt` → `world`, `2`).
- Line numbers shown are the ORIGINAL file line numbers (`--style=numbers` showed 2,3,5,6).
- With grid/snip style, disjoint ranges are separated by a snip line (see 4.3).
- With decorations, an out-of-range selection still prints header+grid, empty body, exit 0.

### 4.2 Errors (stderr, exit 1; message always colored `\e[31m…\e[0m` even when piped)

- `-r abc` / `-r '::'` → `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: invalid digit found in string\n`
- `-r ':'` → `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: cannot parse integer from empty string\n`
- `-r '1:2:3:4'` → `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: Line range contained too many ':' characters. Expected format: 'N', 'N:M', 'N::C', or 'N:M:C'\n`
- `-r ' 3'` (leading space) → `invalid digit found in string` (no trimming)

### 4.3 Snip line (grid style, between disjoint ranges)

Width 80: ` ... │ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ 8< ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─\n`
(number field = right-aligned `...` in 4 chars + ` │ `; content = 35 `─` and 35 spaces
interleaved as `─ `×18? — exact repr: `'─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ 8< ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─'`,
i.e. 18 dashes space-separated, ` 8< `, 17 more space-separated dashes; total content width 72).
Width 20: `' ... │ ─ ─ ─ 8< ─ ─\n'` (content = `─ ─ ─ 8< ─ ─`, 12 chars).
Snip line only appears when the `snip` style component AND grid are active
(default style includes snip; `--style=numbers` alone shows no separator).

## 5. `-H/--highlight-line`

- Same range syntax as `-r` (`40`, `30:40`, `:40`, `40:`, `30:+10` verified) **except**
  negative ranges: `-H '-2:'` → clap error `error: unexpected argument '-2' found` (exit 2),
  while `-r '-2:'` works. Quirk confirmed.
- No effect on the plain piped path.
- Highlighted line: content segments get background prepended per segment:
  `\e[48;5;236;38;5;<fg>m<text>\e[0m` (bg `48;5;236` in both default theme and TwoDark;
  fg is the token's normal color). After the content, the rest of the line is padded with
  spaces in `\e[48;5;236m<spaces>\e[0m` up to the full terminal width (or content-area width
  when a sidebar is present). `\n` after.
- With grid+numbers: the line-number field and `│` separator are NOT highlighted
  (stay `38;5;246`); the space after `│` is not highlighted; content+padding are.
  Width 20: `   2 │ ` then `\e[48;5;236;38;5;231m2\e[0m\e[48;5;236m` + 12 spaces + `\e[0m\n`.
- Empty highlighted line: `\e[48;5;236m` + full-width spaces + `\e[0m\n` (no content segment).
- Wrapped highlighted line: every continuation line gets the bg; only the last (short)
  continuation gets bg padding.
- `-r` and `-H` compose: `-r 5 -H 5` highlights the printed line (original numbering).
- Out-of-range `-H 99`: silently ignored. Invalid `-H abc` →
  `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: invalid digit found in string\n` on stderr, exit 1.

## 6. `-s/--squeeze-blank` and `--squeeze-limit`

- `-s`/`--squeeze-blank`: collapses runs of TRULY EMPTY lines (zero chars before `\n`) to one.
  `a\n\n\n\n\nb\n\n\nc\n` → `a\n\nb\n\nc\n`. Works even on the plain piped path.
- Lines containing only whitespace are NOT blank: `a\n   \n\t\nb\n` unchanged under `-s`.
- `--squeeze-limit N` alone (without `-s`) does nothing (verified N=0,2).
- `-s --squeeze-limit 0`: removes ALL empty lines → `a\nb\nc\n`.
- `-s --squeeze-limit 2`: keeps at most 2 → `a\n\n\nb\n\n\nc\n`.
- Line numbers keep original values when squeezing (`1 a`, `2 ␣`, `6 b`, `7 ␣`, `9 c`).
- `--squeeze-limit -1` → clap `unexpected argument '-1'` error, exit 2.

## 7. `--strip-ansi <when>`

Values `auto`, `always`, `never` (default `never`); invalid value → clap error exit 2.
Only effective on the transforming paths (color/decorations); plain piped path always passes
input ANSI through untouched.

- `never` (default): input escape sequences are kept (see 3.6 for how they are re-emitted
  when coloring). With a real syntax (`-l py`), the raw ESC bytes get tokenized as text and
  re-emitted (messy but preserved).
- `always`: input ANSI stripped before highlighting, even for plain text:
  `\e[31mRED\e[0m normal…` → `\e[38;5;231mRED normal text here ok\e[0m\n`.
- `auto`: strips unless the detected syntax is plain text (auto-detected `.txt` or `-l txt`
  keeps the input ANSI; `-l py` strips).

## 8. Binary, encodings, edge inputs

### 8.1 Binary detection

- A file is "binary" if a NUL (0x00) occurs within the **first 1024 bytes** (offsets 0–1023).
  Verified boundary: NUL at offset 1023 → binary; offset 1024 → not binary.
- UTF-16 files WITH a BOM (FF FE or FE FF) are NOT binary — they are transcoded to UTF-8
  on the transforming paths: `FF FE 68 00 69 00` → `\e[38;5;231mhi\e[0m` (NULs gone,
  no trailing newline added). UTF-16 without BOM → NULs in first 1024 → binary.
- Default `--binary=no-printing` behavior:
  - plain piped path: content printed RAW anyway (NULs included), no warning, exit 0.
    (`hello\x00world\n` → `hello\0world\n`)
  - color path: content suppressed; this warning goes to **stdout** (not stderr!), exit 0:
    `\e[33m[bat warning]\e[0m: Binary content from file 'nul.bin' will not be printed to the terminal (but will be present if the output of 'bat' is piped). You can use 'bat -A' to show the binary file contents.\n`
    For stdin: `… Binary content from STDIN will not be printed …`.
  - decorations path: header line becomes `     │ File: nul.bin   <BINARY>` (3 spaces before
    `<BINARY>`), no content lines, no warning, exit 0.
- `--binary=as-text`: content printed normally everywhere (NULs raw; with decorations the
  NUL passes through into the content line: `   1 │ hello\0world`).
- `-A`: prints binary with the glyph mapping (§1).

### 8.2 Invalid UTF-8

- Plain piped: raw passthrough (`bad \xff\xfe utf8\n` unchanged), exit 0.
- Color path: each invalid byte replaced with U+FFFD (`ef bf bd`), inside the text segment:
  `\e[38;5;231mbad ��� utf8\e[0m\n` (here `��` = 2×U+FFFD), exit 0, no error/warning.

### 8.3 BOM (UTF-8)

- Plain piped: BOM `ef bb bf` passed through.
- Color path: BOM stripped: file `EF BB BF hello\n` → `\e[38;5;231mhello\e[0m\n`.
- `-A`: BOM NOT stripped, shown as `\u{feff}` (see 1.1).

### 8.4 CRLF / lone CR

- Plain piped: `\r\n` passed through raw.
- Color path: line content `line1\r\n` → `\e[38;5;231mline1\e[0m\r\n` — the `\r` is preserved
  but emitted AFTER the `\e[0m`, immediately before `\n`. Mid-line `\r` stays inside the
  colored segment (`a\rb\n` → `\e[38;5;231ma\rb\e[0m\n`). Lines split on `\n` only.

### 8.5 Missing trailing newline

- Plain piped and color path: nothing added — output ends without `\n`
  (`nonl` → `nonl`, color: `\e[38;5;231mnonl\e[0m`).
- Decorations path: a `\n` IS added after the last content line
  (`   1 │ nonl\n` then the bottom grid line).
- `-A`: no `␊` glyph and no `\n` added for the final unterminated line.

### 8.6 Empty input

- Plain piped: zero output, exit 0.
- Decorations: header `     │ File: empty.txt   <EMPTY>` (or `     │ STDIN   <EMPTY>` for
  stdin), top+bottom grid, no content, exit 0.
- `-E/--quiet-empty`: empty input → absolutely no output (not even header), exit 0.

### 8.7 Long lines

1 000 000-char line: printed in full (plain: 1000001 bytes; color+wrap=never: 1000016 =
+15 bytes for the two ANSI sequences). No truncation or performance cutoffs observed.

## 9. Errors & exit codes summary

- clap/usage errors (bad enum value, bad `--terminal-width`, `-1` flags, `-H '-2:'`):
  plain `error: …` text on stderr, exit **2**.
- runtime bat errors (bad `-r`/`-H` range strings): stderr
  `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: <msg>\n` (colored even when piped), exit **1**.
- binary/empty/invalid-UTF-8/out-of-range: all exit **0**.

The spec is complete at `/workspace/specs/content.md`. Here is the 10-line summary of the most important findings:

1. **Three output paths decide everything**: plain-piped (no color, no decorations) = raw byte passthrough where `--tabs`, `--wrap`, `--strip-ansi`, binary suppression, BOM stripping, and invalid-UTF-8 replacement are ALL ignored; only `-r` and `-s` still apply. Color (`--color=always`) and decorations (`--decorations=always`) each activate the transforming printer; `-A` also forces it.
2. **`-A` mapping**: C0 controls → U+2400+cp (`␀`…) or caret `^@`…; DEL → `␡`/`^?`; LF → `␊`+real `\n` (caret `^J`); CR → `␍`/`^M` inline; TAB → box placeholder; space → `·` (U+00B7); and **every** non-ASCII char ≥ U+0080 (even printable `é`, `中`, `😀`, U+00B7 itself) → literal `\u{hex}` lowercase escape. `-A` also disables BOM stripping (`\u{feff}` shown) and overrides binary suppression.
3. **Tab placeholders**: width `w = N − (col mod N)`, default N=4 (even with `--tabs 0` under `-A`); `w=1` → `↹`, `w=2` → `├┤`, else `├`+`─`×(w−2)+`┤`.
4. **Tab expansion quirk**: without `-A`, expansion happens only on decoration paths (default width 4) or when `--tabs N` is explicitly given on the color path; default color-only mode keeps raw `\t`; plain-piped never expands.
5. **`-A` glyph colors** (default theme): text 231, tab placeholder 141, `␊` 203, `␍` 186, `·` 81, `\u{…}` 242; C0/DEL glyphs and caret sequences inherit surrounding text color; all theme-dependent.
6. **Wrapping**: only when color or decorations active; `auto` == `character`; `never` does NOT truncate; char wrap breaks at exact content width (terminal − 7 sidebar); word wrap is greedy-on-spaces with weird space handling at breaks (`aa bb` w=5 → `aa bb`/`␣cc`), no hyphen awareness, no continuation indent; CJK=2 cols, combining=0, input ANSI=0 width; width from `--terminal-width`/`BAT_WIDTH` (offsets relative to 80 when piped), `COLUMNS` ignored.
7. **Line ranges**: 1-based inclusive, `N`, `N:M`, `N:`, `:M`, `N:+M`, `-N:` (last N), `N::C`, `N:M:C`, multiple ranges merge, clamp to EOF, empty/out-of-range → exit 0 with no error; with grid+snip, disjoint ranges separated by ` ... │ ─… 8< …─` (content width = terminal−8); original line numbering preserved.
8. **Highlight-line**: bg `48;5;236` prepended per segment (`\e[48;5;236;38;5;<fg>m`), line padded with bg spaces to full width (content area when sidebar present; number field and `│` NOT highlighted); supports `-r` syntax except negatives (`-H '-2:'` is a clap error while `-r '-2:'` works).
9. **Binary**: NUL in first 1024 bytes = binary; plain-piped prints it raw anyway; color path prints a yellow `[bat warning]: Binary content from file '…' will not be printed…` to **stdout**; decorations show `File: x   <BINARY>` header only; `--binary=as-text`/`-A` print it; UTF-16 with BOM is transcoded to UTF-8, not binary.
10. **Encodings/edges**: invalid UTF-8 → one U+FFFD per bad byte on color path, raw passthrough when piped; UTF-8 BOM stripped on color path only; CRLF keeps `\r` (emitted after `\e[0m` before `\n`); missing trailing newline NOT added on plain/color paths but IS added with decorations; empty input → zero output plain, `<EMPTY>` header with decorations, nothing at all with `-E`; squeeze only collapses truly empty lines, `--squeeze-limit` inert without `-s`; bat runtime errors are `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: …` exit 1, clap errors exit 2.

args.content:
# Spec: Syntax highlighting & language detection (bat 0.26.1)

Recon area: `--list-languages`, language auto-detection (extension / filename / glob / first-line /
shebang), `-l`/`--language`, `--map-syntax`/`-m`, `--fallback-syntax`, `--ignored-suffix`, and the
exact ANSI bytes of highlighted output.

All probes were run against `./executable` (bat 0.26.1 (610b77c)) with a controlled environment
unless noted otherwise:

```
env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=/tmp/fakehome TERM=xterm ./executable ...
```

In this environment: COLORTERM unset → 256-color output; COLORTERM=truecolor → 24-bit output.
Default theme in this environment is the dark Monokai-Extended-style theme (fg = `38;5;231`,
truecolor fg = `38;2;248;248;242`). Theme selection itself is another agent's area; all byte-level
results below assume this default theme. Note `HOME=/tmp/fakehome` matters: some
`--list-languages` entries embed `$HOME` (see below).

"stdout piped" is the judge's normal mode: colors/decorations default to OFF when stdout is not a
tty, so most highlighting probes were done with `--color=always --style=plain`.

---

## 1. `--list-languages` / `-L`

- Alias: `-L`. Exit code 0. Extra positional args are ignored (`bat --list-languages somefile`
  still prints the list, rc=0).
- Output: 183 lines, one per syntax, format `Name:ext1,ext2,...` (no spaces around `:` or `,`).
  Sorted alphabetically by syntax name (case-insensitively: "CpuInfo" between "Command Help" and
  "Crontab", lowercase names like `fstab`, `group`, `jsonnet`, `log`, `passwd`, `resolv`, `syslog`,
  `varlink` sort among the capitalized ones).
- Lines for syntaxes with NO extensions end with a bare colon, e.g. `NAnt Build File:` — wait,
  actually observed `NAnt Build File:` has no extensions listed (prints just the name and colon)...
  correction: it prints `NAnt Build File:` only when `-m` mappings add entries; the stock entry is
  `NAnt Build File:build`. See the captured file.
- Full captured output: `specs/list-languages.HOME-is-tmp-fakehome.txt` (verbatim, 183 lines).
- HOME-dependent entries (verbatim with HOME=/tmp/fakehome; the `$HOME` prefix changes with HOME):
  - `Git Attributes:...,/tmp/fakehome/.config/git/attributes`
  - `Git Config:gitconfig,.gitconfig,.gitmodules,/tmp/fakehome/.config/git/config`
  - `Git Ignore:exclude,gitignore,.gitignore,.gcloudignore,/tmp/fakehome/.config/git/ignore,.?*ignore`
  - `TOML:...,/tmp/fakehome/.config/containers/**/*.conf`
  (With HOME=/root these become `/root/.config/git/...` etc.)
- Custom `-m` mappings are folded INTO this list: `-m '*.build:Python' --list-languages` shows
  `Python:py,py3,...,bzl,*.build,BUILD,...` — the custom glob is appended after the last
  non-`BUILD` token (`bzl`) and before `BUILD`. (i.e. inserted into that syntax's extension list.)
- Notable mappings (verbatim from capture; complete list in the txt file):
  - `Plain Text:txt` — only `txt`.
  - `C:c`, `C++:cpp,cc,cp,cxx,c++,h,hh,hpp,hxx,h++,inl,ipp,*.h` (so `.h` → C++, not C).
  - `Bourne Again Shell (bash):sh,bash,zsh,ash,...` (many globs incl. `**/bat/config`).
  - `JavaScript:htc`; `JavaScript (Babel):js,mjs,jsx,babel,es6,cjs,*.pac` (so `.js` →
    "JavaScript (Babel)").
  - `TypeScript:ts,mts,cts`, `TypeScriptReact:tsx`.
  - `Dockerfile:Dockerfile,dockerfile,.Dockerfile,Containerfile`
  - `Makefile:make,GNUmakefile,makefile,Makefile,makefile.am,Makefile.am,makefile.in,Makefile.in,OCamlMakefile,mak,mk`
  - `CMake:CMakeLists.txt,cmake`; `CMake C Header:h.in`; `CMake C++ Header:hh.in,hpp.in,hxx.in,h++.in`.
  - `Diff:diff,patch,*.debdiff`; `YAML:yaml,yml,...`; `TOML:toml,tml,Cargo.lock,...`;
    `INI:ini,INI,inf,INF,reg,REG,lng,cfg,CFG,...`; `JSON:json,...`; `Markdown:md,mdown,markdown,markdn,*.mkd`.
  - `Python:py,py3,pyw,pyi,pyx,pyx.in,pxd,pxd.in,pxi,pxi.in,rpy,cpy,SConstruct,...`;
    `Perl:pl,pc,pm,pmc,pod,t`; `Ruby:rb,...`; `VimL:vim,vimrc,...`; `Lua:lua,*.nse`;
    `SQL:sql,ddl,dml`; `Pascal:pas,p,dpr`; `R:R,r,Rprofile`; `ARM Assembly:s,S`;
    `Go:go`; `Java:java,bsh`; `Rust:rs,*.ron`; `Fish:fish`; `DotENV:.env,...`;
    `Groff/troff:groff,troff,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9` (so `foo.1`…`foo.9` → man-page syntax).

## 2. Detection pipeline (empirically derived order)

For each input file, syntax is resolved in this order; first hit wins:

1. `-l`/`--language` if given (see §4). Applies to ALL inputs.
2. Custom `-m`/`--map-syntax` mappings (see §5). Tried against the original name and against the
   suffix-stripped name (see below), each as both bare filename and full path.
3. Filename/extension match against the syntax set (details §3), after recursively stripping
   "ignored suffixes" (§3.3). Case-insensitive.
4. First-line detection (§3.4) — only if step 3 found nothing.
5. `--fallback-syntax` (§6) — only if steps 1–4 found nothing.
6. `Plain Text`.

Additional facts:

- Extension match BEATS first-line detection: a file `x.txt` containing `#!/bin/bash\necho hi`
  renders as Plain Text; `x.py` with a bash shebang renders as Python.
- First-line detection also runs for stdin with no filename
  (`printf '#!/bin/bash\necho hi\n' | bat -` → bash-highlighted).
- `--file-name <name>` on stdin drives detection exactly like a real filename
  (`--file-name x.py` → Python; `--file-name x.zzz` + bash shebang → bash;
  `--file-name x.txt` + bash shebang → Plain Text).
- Detection is per-file when multiple files are given.
- The syntax set's own glob tokens (e.g. `**/bat/config`, `.?*ignore`, `*.bashrc`) are matched at
  any depth: both `bat/config` and `deep/a/bat/config` (relative paths) detect bash; a file named
  just `config` does not. `.eslintignore` → Git Ignore (via `.?*ignore`); `x.eslintignore` and
  `foo.ignore` do NOT (the token requires a leading `.`).

### 3.1 Extension/filename matching

- Case-INSENSITIVE, for both extensions and full-filename tokens:
  `probe.RS`→Rust, `x.C`→C, `x.SH`→bash, `x.PY`→Python, `x.JSON`/`x.Json`→JSON,
  `MAKEFILE`→Makefile, `cmakelists.txt`→CMake. (Tokens `S`/`S` etc. exist anyway, but `RS`, `PY`,
  `C` are not tokens — case folding is real.)
- The whole filename is tried as a token too (this is how `Makefile`, `Dockerfile`,
  `CMakeLists.txt`, `.bashrc` work), AND the last `.`-suffix as extension, AND glob tokens.
  Consequence: a file named exactly `r` detects as `R` (token `r`); a file named `s` detects as
  `ARM Assembly` (token `s`); `1`–`9` as Groff/troff.
- Verified extension → syntax (forced-`-l` output equality, representative content):
  rs→Rust, py→Python, js→JavaScript (Babel), ts→TypeScript, c→C, cpp/h/hpp→C++, java→Java,
  go→Go, rb→Ruby, sh/bash/zsh→Bourne Again Shell (bash), fish→Fish, json→JSON, yaml/yml→YAML,
  toml→TOML, xml→XML, html→HTML, css→CSS, md→Markdown, txt→Plain Text, pl→Perl, php→PHP,
  lua→Lua, sql→SQL, vim→VimL, dockerfile→Dockerfile, makefile/mk→Makefile, cmake→CMake,
  ini/cfg→INI, diff/patch→Diff, pas→Pascal.
- Verified filename tokens: `Dockerfile`, `dockerfile`, `.Dockerfile` → Dockerfile;
  `Makefile`, `makefile`, `GNUmakefile`, `makefile.am` → Makefile; `CMakeLists.txt` → CMake;
  `.bashrc`, `.zshrc`, `z.bashrc` (via `*.bashrc`) → bash; `.env` → DotENV;
  `x.h.in` → CMake C Header; `x.hpp.in` → CMake C++ Header; `Containerfile` (token listed).
- Filename tokens are NOT prefix/substring matches: `Dockerfilefoo`, `xDockerfile`,
  `CMakeListsfoo.txt`, `zzCMakeLists.txt`, `CMakeLists.txt2`, `Makefilefoo`, `xMakefile` all
  detect as Plain Text (given non-first-line-triggering content). (Beware: several earlier
  apparent matches were actually first-line detection, §3.4.)

### 3.2 Unknown extension

- Unknown extension (e.g. `.xyzunknown`, `.qqq`) and no extension → Plain Text, output
  byte-identical to `-l txt`. (Unless first-line or fallback kicks in.)

### 3.3 Built-in ignored suffixes (backup files)

Before matching, these trailing suffixes are stripped, RECURSIVELY, case-SENSITIVELY:

```
~  bak  old  orig
dpkg-old  dpkg-new  dpkg-tmp  dpkg-dist
ucf-old   ucf-new   ucf-dist
rpmsave   rpmnew    rpmorig
```

Verified stripped: `x.rs.bak`, `x.rs.orig`, `x.rs.old`, `x.rs~`, `x.rs~~`, `x.rs~.bak`,
`x.rs.bak.bak`, `Makefile.bak/.orig/.old`, `Makefile~`, `x.mk.bak`, `x.css.bak`, `.bashrc.bak`,
`CMakeLists.txt.bak`, `x.rs.dpkg-old/-new/-tmp/-dist`, `x.rs.ucf-old/-new/-dist`,
`x.rs.rpmsave/.rpmnew/.rpmorig` (all detect the underlying syntax).
Verified NOT stripped: `.dev .tmp .swp .swo .sav .save .rej .bk .backup .pacsave .pacnew .pacorig
.new .dist .tmp .apt .bak1 .old2 .oldbak .orig2 .BAK .OLD .Orig .un~` (all → Plain Text on
`x.rs.<sfx>`).
- `Makefile.bak.txt` → Plain Text (`.txt` is a real extension; no stripping of `.txt`).
- Stripping interacts with first-line detection: `zz.bak` (no ext after strip) + ruby shebang →
  Ruby; `s.bak` → `s` → ARM Assembly (before first-line is even consulted).

### 3.4 First-line / shebang detection

Applied only when filename/extension matching found nothing (incl. extensionless files and stdin
without `--file-name`).

Verified triggers (extensionless file unless noted):

| first line | detected |
|---|---|
| `#!/bin/bash`, `#!/bin/sh`, `#!/usr/bin/zsh`, `#!/usr/bin/bash`, `#!/bin/ash`, `#!/bin/dash`, `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, `#!/bin/bash -e`, `#! /bin/bash` (space after `#!`) | Bourne Again Shell (bash) |
| `#!/usr/bin/env python3`, `#!/usr/bin/env python`, `#!/usr/bin/python2`, `#!/usr/bin/env python3 -u`, `#!/usr/bin/env -S python3 -u`, `#!/usr/bin/env python3.12`, `#!/bin/env python3` | Python |
| `#!/usr/bin/perl` | Perl |
| `#!/usr/bin/env ruby` | Ruby |
| `#!/usr/bin/env node` | JavaScript (Babel) |
| `#!/usr/bin/fish` | Fish |
| `#!/usr/bin/env php` | PHP |
| `#!/usr/bin/make -f` | Makefile |
| `FROM x` (Dockerfile, even in `c1.unkext`) | Dockerfile |
| `<?php ...` (also leading space ` <?php`, also bare `<?`) | PHP |
| `<?xml version="1.0"?>` | XML |
| `<!DOCTYPE html>` (any case), `<html>` | HTML |

Verified NON-triggers (→ Plain Text):

- `#!/usr/bin/lua`, `#!/usr/bin/env lua`, `#!/usr/bin/env -S lua` (Lua has no first-line match)
- `#!/usr/bin/perl5` (word boundary required), `#!/bin/bashe`, `#!/bin/shx`
- `#!/usr/bin/env gawk`, `#!/usr/bin/awk -f`, `#!/usr/bin/env tclsh`, `#!/usr/bin/env Rscript`,
  `#!/usr/bin/env groovy`
- `#!` alone; `#!/usr/bin/env` alone
- Shebang on line 2 (first line empty) → no detection; leading space before `#!` → no detection.
- `all:\n\techo` (Makefile-looking content) → no first-line detection.
- `cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)` → no first-line detection.
- `COPY a b` / `EXPOSE 80` as first line → NOT Dockerfile (only `^FROM ` triggers it).

Other details:

- CRLF after shebang (`#!/bin/bash\r\n`) still detects bash.
- UTF-8 BOM before `#!` still detects bash (BOM is stripped before first-line matching).
- `.txt` extension beats all first-line triggers (`x.txt` + `<?php` → Plain Text; `x.txt` +
  `<?xml` → Plain Text; `x.txt` + shebang → Plain Text).
- Word-boundary behavior: `python3`, `python3.12`, `python2` match; `perl5` does not.

## 4. `-l` / `--language`

- Accepts a syntax NAME (exact, case-insensitive; e.g. `Rust`, `rust`, `C++`, `c++`,
  `Bourne Again Shell (bash)`, `bourne again shell (bash)`, `plain text`, `git config`,
  `JavaScript (Babel)`) or an EXTENSION TOKEN (case-insensitive: `rs`, `RS`, `py`, `cpp`, `CPP`,
  `h` → C++, `js` → JavaScript (Babel), `txt` → Plain Text, `dockerfile`, `gitconfig`).
- Dotted tokens that exist in the list work: `-l .bashrc` → bash. But `-l .rs` fails (token is
  `rs`, no dot). So: exact token match including any leading dot; no stripping of a leading `.`.
- No substring/prefix matching (`shel`, `Bourne Again Shell` fail), no whitespace trimming
  (`-l ' Markdown'`, `-l 'Markdown '` fail).
- `-l c` → C (not C++); `-l m` resolves (Objective-C; output identical to C++ for trivial
  content); `-l s` → ARM Assembly; `-l v` → Verilog; `-l show-nonprintable` works (special
  "Highlight non-printables" syntax).
- Forms: `-l rust`, `-lrust`, `--language rust`, `--language=rust` all work.
- Repeated `-l`: LAST one wins (`-l Rust -l Python` → Python).
- Invalid language, highlighting ENABLED (`--color=always` or `-f`): exit code 1, empty stdout,
  stderr exactly (ANSI even when piped):

  ```
  \e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: unknown syntax: '<value>\n
  ```

  e.g. `-l python3` → `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: unknown syntax: 'python3'\n`; `-l ''` →
  `...unknown syntax: ''\n`.
- Invalid language, highlighting DISABLED (piped default, `--color=never`, `--color=auto` piped,
  `NO_COLOR=1`, `--style=plain` alone, `--decorations=always` alone): NO error, exit 0, file
  printed raw (no colors). I.e. the syntax lookup error only fires when colorization is active.
- With multiple input files and a bad `-l` (colors on): the error line is printed once PER INPUT
  FILE (`-l nope a b` → two identical error lines), stdout empty, rc=1.

## 5. `--map-syntax` / `-m <glob>:<syntax>`

- Format error (missing colon, empty string, or more than one colon — `a:b:c`): exit 1, stderr
  exactly (even with `--color=never`; this is a startup parse error):

  ```
  \e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: Invalid syntax mapping. The format of the -m/--map-syntax option is '<glob-pattern>:<syntax-name>'. For example: '*.cpp:C++'.\n
  ```

- Right-hand side: syntax name (case-insensitive) OR extension token — `-m '*.build:python'` and
  `-m '*.build:py'` both work. Unknown target WITH colors on: exit 1,
  `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: unknown syntax: '<name>'\n` (e.g. `-m '*.build:NoSuch'`).
  Unknown target with colors OFF (piped default / `--color=never`): silently accepted, rc=0
  (same lazy behavior as `-l`). `-m '*.build:'` → `unknown syntax: ''` (colors on).
- `-m ':Python'` (empty glob) is ACCEPTED (rc=0) and matches nothing.
- Glob semantics (globset-style):
  - Matched case-INSENSITIVELY (`*.BUILD` matches `t.build`).
  - Matched against the bare filename AND the full path (`*` does not cross `/`, `**` does):
    `*build` matches `t.build`; `?.build` matches `t.build`; `**/t.build` matches;
    `/tmp/**` and `/tmp/recon-hl/map/*` match `/tmp/recon-hl/map/t.build` even when the argument
    is given as a relative path; `*/map/*` does NOT match `/tmp/recon-hl/map/t.build`
    (one `*` ≠ two components); `*/t.build` does not match.
  - A non-glob pattern like `build` matches only a file named exactly `build` (NOT `t.build`).
  - Mapping globs are also tried against the suffix-stripped name: with
    `--ignored-suffix .dev`, both `-m '*.dev:Python'` (matches original `my_file.json.dev`) and
    `-m '*.json:Python'` (matches stripped `my_file.json`) apply.
- Precedence: `-l` beats `-m`; `-m` beats built-in extension detection
  (`-m '*.rs:Python' t.rs` → Python; `rs:Python` does NOT remap the `.rs` extension — the pattern
  is a filename glob, not an extension shorthand). Built-in filename/ext detection beats
  first-line, which beats `--fallback-syntax`.
- Multiple `-m`: LAST matching mapping wins
  (`-m '*.build:Python' -m '*.build:Rust'` → Rust; reversed → Python).
- `-m '*.build:Plain Text'` works (forces plain).
- `-m` mappings appear in `--list-languages` output (see §1).

## 6. `--fallback-syntax` (alias `--fallback-language`)

- Used ONLY when nothing else matched (unknown extension, extensionless without shebang, or stdin
  without filename/shebang). Known extensions beat it; first-line detection beats it; `-m` and
  `-l` beat it. E.g. `--fallback-syntax Rust t3.txt` → Plain Text; shebang file + fallback →
  shebang's syntax.
- Accepts name or extension, case-insensitive (`Rust`, `rust`, `rs`, `INI`, `ini` all work).
  `--fallback-syntax=Rust` form works.
- Works for stdin: `printf 'x=1\n' | bat --color=always --style=plain --fallback-syntax INI -`
  produces INI highlighting.
- Invalid value, and the fallback is actually NEEDED, colors on: exit 1, stdout empty, stderr
  `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: unknown syntax: '<value>'\n`. If the fallback is not needed (known
  extension etc.), an invalid value is silently ignored, rc=0. `--fallback-syntax ''` on an
  undetectable file → `unknown syntax: ''`, rc=1.

## 7. `--ignored-suffix <suffix>`

- Example from docs works: `--ignored-suffix .dev my_file.json.dev` → JSON.
- The suffix must include the leading dot (`--ignored-suffix dev` has no effect) and is
  case-SENSITIVE (`.DEV` ≠ `.dev`).
- Can be repeated; applied recursively (`f.json.dev.dev` + one `--ignored-suffix .dev` → JSON);
  composes with the built-in suffixes (`f.json.dev.bak` + `--ignored-suffix .dev` → JSON).
- If after stripping nothing resolves, the ORIGINAL name's detection still applies
  (`--ignored-suffix .rs g.rs` → still Rust, not Plain).
- Stripping precedes first-line detection (a stripped-to-no-extension name can still be detected
  by shebang) and interacts with whole-filename tokens (`--ignored-suffix .sh r.sh` → filename
  `r` → R syntax!).
- Does not affect `-l`.
- BUG: `--ignored-suffix ''` (empty string) crashes: exit code 134 (SIGABRT), stderr:
  `thread 'main' (<pid>) has overflowed its stack\nfatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting\n`
  (pid varies).

## 8. Exact output bytes (default theme, default env)

### Plain Text / unhighlighted

`printf 'hello world\nsecond line\n' > plain.txt; bat --color=always --style=plain plain.txt`:

```
\e[38;5;231mhello world\e[0m\n\e[38;5;231msecond line\e[0m\n
```

With `COLORTERM=truecolor`:

```
\e[38;2;248;248;242mhello world\e[0m\n\e[38;2;248;248;242msecond line\e[0m\n
```

Rules:
- Every non-empty line: `<SGR fg>` + raw line bytes + `\e[0m`, then `\n`. Reset comes BEFORE the
  newline; newline itself is uncolored.
- Empty lines are emitted as a bare `\n` (no SGR at all).
- A final line without trailing newline gets no `\n`; output ends after its `\e[0m`
  (`printf 'a\n\nb'` → `\e[38;5;231ma\e[0m\n\n\e[38;5;231mb\e[0m`).
- Unknown-extension output is byte-identical to `-l txt` output.
- Default piped invocation (no flags, stdout not a tty): output is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the input
  file (no colors, no decorations) for all corpus samples. rc=0.
- `--theme=ansi` with Plain Text: no SGR sequences at all, raw passthrough.

### Highlighted (tokenized) languages

- Output is a sequence of `\e[38;5;<n>m<text>\e[0m` spans; spans are per-token and often split
  around single characters (e.g. Rust: `\e[38;5;81mfn\e[0m\e[38;5;231m \e[0m\e[38;5;149mmain...`).
  There is no span merging — adjacent same-color tokens may still be separate spans (e.g.
  `\e[38;5;242m//\e[0m\e[38;5;242m answer\e[0m`).
- Same line rules as Plain Text: reset before `\n`, bare `\n` for empty lines.
- 256-color palette observed with default theme (Monokai-Extended-like): fg 231, comments 242
  (bash comments 243), keywords 81, strings 186, numbers/constants 141, function names 149,
  operators/diff-deleted 203, diff-added 149, diff hunk headers 75. Truecolor equivalents appear
  in the `*.expected-truecolor` corpus files (e.g. fg `38;2;248;248;242`).
- `--italic-text=always` adds `3;` to the SGR for scopes the theme marks italic, e.g. Rust `fn`
  becomes `\e[3;38;5;81mfn\e[0m`. Default is `--italic-text=never`.
- Dockerfile quirk: instruction keywords are only highlighted AFTER a `FROM` instruction; a file
  starting with `RUN ...` (no `FROM`) highlights nothing except `#` comments (242).

### Regression corpus

`tests/corpus/` contains `sample.{txt,rs,py,sh,c,json,yaml,md,toml,diff}` (3–8 lines each) and,
per file:

- `<name>.expected` — `env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=/tmp/fakehome TERM=xterm ./executable
  --color=always --style=plain <file>` (COLORTERM unset → 256-color), rc=0.
- `<name>.expected-truecolor` — same with `COLORTERM=truecolor`, rc=0.
- `<name>.expected-default` — same env, NO flags, stdout piped: byte-identical to the input
  (verified with `cmp`), rc=0.

Example (diff, 256-color): `--- a/hello.txt` →
`\e[38;5;242m---\e[0m\e[38;5;242m a/hello.txt\e[0m\n` + hunk header spans in 75, `-` lines in 203,
`+` lines in 149, context lines in 231.

## 9. Errors & warnings cheat-sheet (this area)

| condition | rc | stdout | stderr (exact) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-l <bad>`, colors on | 1 | empty | `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: unknown syntax: '<bad>'\n` (once per input file) |
| `-l <bad>`, colors off/piped | 0 | raw file | empty |
| `-m` bad format (`nocolon`, ``, `a:b:c`) | 1 | empty | `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: Invalid syntax mapping. The format of the -m/--map-syntax option is '<glob-pattern>:<syntax-name>'. For example: '*.cpp:C++'.\n` (always, even `--color=never`) |
| `-m '*:BadName'`, colors on | 1 | empty | `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: unknown syntax: 'BadName'\n` |
| `-m '*:BadName'`, colors off | 0 | raw file | empty |
| `--fallback-syntax <bad>`, fallback needed, colors on | 1 | empty | `\e[31m[bat error]\e[0m: unknown syntax: '<bad>'\n` |
| `--fallback-syntax <bad>`, fallback not needed | 0 | normal | empty |
| `--ignored-suffix ''` | 134 | empty | `thread 'main' (<pid>) has overflowed its stack\nfatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting\n` |
| `--theme <bad>`, colors on | 0 | normal output | `\e[33m[bat warning]\e[0m: Unknown theme '<bad>', using default.\n` (recorded for completeness; theme area) |

Note: `[bat error]`/`[bat warning]` lines are ANSI-colored on stderr even when stdout is piped
(whenever they are emitted at all).
